decls.name: closureB
decls.doc: Every node the map links to the gene is in the change set.
decls.statement:
def closureB (mapped changed : List String) : Bool := mapped.all fun n => changed.contains n

theorem closure_of_check {mapped changed : List String} (h : closureB mapped changed = true) :
    ∀ n ∈ mapped, n ∈ changed

decls.name: closure_of_check
decls.statement:
theorem closure_of_check {mapped changed : List String} (h : closureB mapped changed = true) :
    ∀ n ∈ mapped, n ∈ changed

decls.name: closure_violated
decls.doc: A change set that omits a mapped node violates closure.
decls.statement:
theorem closure_violated {mapped changed : List String} {n : String} (hn : n ∈ mapped) (hc : n ∉ changed) :
    closureB mapped changed = false

decls.name: expectedWaitingTime
decls.doc: Expected generations for `N` sequential independent fixations at rate `M μ u` each (a definition).
decls.statement:
noncomputable def expectedWaitingTime (N : ℝ) (M : ℕ) (μ u : ℝ) : ℝ := N / (substitutionRate M μ u)

theorem expectedWaitingTime_neutral (N : ℝ) (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) :
    expectedWaitingTime N M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) = N / μ

decls.name: expectedWaitingTime_neutral
decls.statement:
theorem expectedWaitingTime_neutral (N : ℝ) (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) :
    expectedWaitingTime N M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) = N / μ

decls.name: expectedWaitingTime_bounds
decls.doc: With `1/M ≤ u ≤ 1`, the waiting time lies between `N/(M μ)` and `N/μ`.

decls.name: too_little_time_rules_out
decls.doc: **Too little time.** An available time `T` below `N/(M μ)` cannot suffice even if every mutant fixed.

decls.name: HaldaneCost
decls.doc: **Haldane's cost of selection, as a named hypothesis**: substitutions by selection over `T` generations are at most `e T / c` (reproductive excess `e`, cost per substitution `c`).
decls.statement:
def HaldaneCost (subs T e c : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < c ∧ 0 ≤ e ∧ subs ≤ e * T / c

/-- Under Haldane's hypothesis, `N` selected substitutions need at least `c N / e` generations. -/
theorem haldane_time_lower {N T e c : ℝ} (h : HaldaneCost N T e c) (he : 0 < e) : c * N / e ≤ T

decls.name: haldane_time_lower
decls.doc: Under Haldane's hypothesis, `N` selected substitutions need at least `c N / e` generations.
decls.statement: theorem haldane_time_lower {N T e c : ℝ} (h : HaldaneCost N T e c) (he : 0 < e) : c * N / e ≤ T

decls.name: haldane_rules_out
decls.statement: theorem haldane_rules_out {N T e c : ℝ} (h : HaldaneCost N T e c) (he : 0 < e) (hT : T < c * N / e) : False

decls.name: NeutralChain
decls.doc: A neutral, absorbing Markov chain on `Fin (M+1)`: the number of mutant gene copies among `M`. `P i j` is the probability of going from `i` copies to `j` copies in one generation.
decls.statement: structure NeutralChain (M : ℕ)

decls.name: pow_nonneg
decls.statement: lemma pow_nonneg (t : ℕ) (i j : Fin (M + 1)) : 0 ≤ (C.P ^ t) i j

decls.name: pow_rowSum
decls.statement: lemma pow_rowSum (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) : ∑ j, (C.P ^ t) i j = 1

decls.name: pow_neutral
decls.statement:
lemma pow_neutral (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    ∑ j, (C.P ^ t) i j * ((j : ℕ) : ℝ) = ((i : ℕ) : ℝ)

decls.name: interior
decls.doc: The intermediate (transient) states: neither lost nor fixed.
decls.statement: def interior (M : ℕ) : Finset (Fin (M + 1))

decls.name: mem_interior
decls.statement: lemma mem_interior {j : Fin (M + 1)} : j ∈ interior M ↔ j ≠ 0 ∧ j ≠ Fin.last M

decls.name: zero_ne_last
decls.statement: lemma zero_ne_last (hM : 0 < M) : (0 : Fin (M + 1)) ≠ Fin.last M

decls.name: sum_split
decls.doc: Splitting a sum over all states into the two absorbing states and the interior.
decls.statement:
lemma sum_split (hM : 0 < M) (f : Fin (M + 1) → ℝ) :
    ∑ j, f j = f 0 + f (Fin.last M) + ∑ j ∈ interior M, f j

decls.name: exists_contraction
decls.doc: Probability of leaving the interior in one step is at most `ρ < 1`, uniformly.
decls.statement:
lemma exists_contraction (hM : 0 < M) :
    ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 ≤ ρ ∧ ρ < 1 ∧ ∀ k ∈ interior M, ∑ j ∈ interior M, C.P k j ≤ ρ

decls.name: unresolved
decls.doc: Probability of being in the interior after `t` generations, starting from `i`.
decls.statement:
def unresolved (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) : ℝ := ∑ j ∈ interior M, (C.P ^ t) i j

lemma unresolved_nonneg (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) : 0 ≤ C.unresolved t i

decls.name: unresolved_nonneg
decls.statement: lemma unresolved_nonneg (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) : 0 ≤ C.unresolved t i

decls.name: unresolved_le_one
decls.statement: lemma unresolved_le_one (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) : C.unresolved t i ≤ 1

decls.name: absorbing_sum_interior
decls.doc: Absorbing states never re-enter the interior.
decls.statement:
lemma absorbing_sum_interior (k : Fin (M + 1)) (hk : k = 0 ∨ k = Fin.last M) :
    ∑ j ∈ interior M, C.P k j = 0

decls.name: unresolved_succ_le
decls.doc: The unresolved probability contracts by `ρ` every generation.

decls.name: unresolved_le_pow
decls.statement:
lemma unresolved_le_pow (hM : 0 < M) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ0 : 0 ≤ ρ)
    (hρ : ∀ k ∈ interior M, ∑ j ∈ interior M, C.P k j ≤ ρ) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    C.unresolved t i ≤ ρ ^ t

decls.name: fixedBy
decls.doc: Probability that a lineage starting from `i` copies is fixed (all `M` copies) by generation `t`.
decls.statement:
def fixedBy (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) : ℝ := (C.P ^ t) i (Fin.last M)

/-- Conservation of the mean splits as: `M · P(fixed by t) + E[copies · 1{unresolved}] = i`. -/
lemma mean_decomposition (hM : 0 < M) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    (M : ℝ) * C.fixedBy t i + ∑ j ∈ interior M, (C.P ^ t) i j * ((j : ℕ) : ℝ)
      = ((i : ℕ) : ℝ)

decls.name: mean_decomposition
decls.doc: Conservation of the mean splits as: `M · P(fixed by t) + E[copies · 1{unresolved}] = i`.
decls.statement:
lemma mean_decomposition (hM : 0 < M) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    (M : ℝ) * C.fixedBy t i + ∑ j ∈ interior M, (C.P ^ t) i j * ((j : ℕ) : ℝ)
      = ((i : ℕ) : ℝ)

decls.name: fixedBy_sub_le_unresolved
decls.doc: The error of `fixedBy` against `i / M` is at most the unresolved probability.
decls.statement:
lemma fixedBy_sub_le_unresolved (hM : 0 < M) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    |C.fixedBy t i - ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M| ≤ C.unresolved t i

decls.name: fixedBy_sub_le
decls.doc: **Neutral fixation probability (quantitative form).** For some `ρ < 1`, the probability of fixation by generation `t` is within `ρ ^ t` of `i / M`.
decls.statement:
theorem fixedBy_sub_le (hM : 0 < M) :
    ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 ≤ ρ ∧ ρ < 1 ∧
      ∀ t (i : Fin (M + 1)), |C.fixedBy t i - ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M| ≤ ρ ^ t

decls.name: fixedBy_tendsto
decls.doc: **Neutral fixation probability (Kimura 1962, neutral case).** A neutral lineage that starts with `i` of `M` copies is eventually fixed with probability `i / M`.
decls.statement:
theorem fixedBy_tendsto (hM : 0 < M) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    Tendsto (fun t => C.fixedBy t i) atTop (𝓝 (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M))

decls.name: fixationProbability
decls.doc: The fixation probability of a lineage starting from `i` copies: the limit of `fixedBy`.
decls.statement: noncomputable def fixationProbability (i : Fin (M + 1)) : ℝ

decls.name: fixationProbability_eq
decls.statement:
theorem fixationProbability_eq (hM : 0 < M) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    C.fixationProbability i = ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M

decls.name: wfKernel
decls.doc: Wright–Fisher sampling: with `i` mutant copies among `M`, the next generation has `j` mutant copies with probability `C(M, j) (i/M)^j (1 - i/M)^(M-j)`.
decls.statement: noncomputable def wfKernel (M : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin (M + 1)) (Fin (M + 1)) ℝ

decls.name: wfKernel_eq_bernstein
decls.statement:
lemma wfKernel_eq_bernstein (i j : Fin (M + 1)) :
    wfKernel M i j = (bernsteinPolynomial ℝ M j).eval (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M)

decls.name: wf_p_nonneg
decls.statement: lemma wf_p_nonneg (i : Fin (M + 1)) : 0 ≤ ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M

decls.name: wf_p_le_one
decls.statement: lemma wf_p_le_one (hM : 0 < M) (i : Fin (M + 1)) : ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M ≤ 1

decls.name: wf_rowSum
decls.statement: lemma wf_rowSum (i : Fin (M + 1)) : ∑ j, wfKernel M i j = 1

decls.name: wf_neutral
decls.statement:
lemma wf_neutral (hM : 0 < M) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    ∑ j, wfKernel M i j * ((j : ℕ) : ℝ) = ((i : ℕ) : ℝ)

decls.name: wf_absorb_zero
decls.statement:
lemma wf_absorb_zero (j : Fin (M + 1)) :
    wfKernel M 0 j = if j = 0 then 1 else 0

decls.name: wf_absorb_last
decls.statement:
lemma wf_absorb_last (hM : 0 < M) (j : Fin (M + 1)) :
    wfKernel M (Fin.last M) j = if j = Fin.last M then 1 else 0

decls.name: wf_escape
decls.statement:
lemma wf_escape (hM : 0 < M) (i : Fin (M + 1)) (_hi0 : i ≠ 0) (hiM : i ≠ Fin.last M) :
    0 < wfKernel M i 0 + wfKernel M i (Fin.last M)

decls.name: wrightFisher
decls.doc: The neutral Wright–Fisher chain on `M` gene copies.
decls.statement: noncomputable def wrightFisher (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) : NeutralChain M

decls.name: oneCopy
decls.doc: A single new mutant: one copy among `M`.
decls.statement:
def oneCopy (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) : Fin (M + 1) := ⟨1, by omega⟩

/-- **Wright–Fisher fixation probability of a new neutral mutant is `1 / M`.** -/
theorem wrightFisher_fixation_one (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) :
    (wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM) = 1 / M

decls.name: wrightFisher_fixation_one
decls.doc: **Wright–Fisher fixation probability of a new neutral mutant is `1 / M`.**
decls.statement:
theorem wrightFisher_fixation_one (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) :
    (wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM) = 1 / M

decls.name: substitutionRate
decls.doc: Kimura's substitution rate: `M μ` new mutants arise per generation (mutation rate `μ` per copy), and each is fixed with probability `u`. The rate of substitution is their product. This is the definition in Kimura (1968), eq. for `k`; it assumes mutants' fates are independent.
decls.statement:
def substitutionRate (M : ℕ) (μ u : ℝ) : ℝ := (M : ℝ) * μ * u

/-- **Kimura (1968).** Under neutral Wright–Fisher evolution, the substitution rate equals
the mutation rate, for every population size `M`. -/
theorem neutral_substitution_rate (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) :
    substitutionRate M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) = μ

decls.name: neutral_substitution_rate
decls.doc: **Kimura (1968).** Under neutral Wright–Fisher evolution, the substitution rate equals the mutation rate, for every population size `M`.
decls.statement:
theorem neutral_substitution_rate (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) :
    substitutionRate M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) = μ

decls.name: neutral_substitution_rate_diploid
decls.doc: The same statement for a diploid population of `N` individuals (`M = 2N` gene copies): `k = 2Nμ · 1/(2N) = μ`, exactly the formula in the claim's notation.
decls.statement:
theorem neutral_substitution_rate_diploid (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (μ : ℝ) :
    substitutionRate (2 * N) μ
      ((wrightFisher (2 * N) (by omega)).fixationProbability (oneCopy (2 * N) (by omega))) = μ

decls.name: neutral_substitution_rate_tendsto
decls.doc: Limit form, with no `limUnder`: the expected number of substitutions per generation attributable to mutants that are fixed by generation `t` converges to `μ`.
decls.statement:
theorem neutral_substitution_rate_tendsto (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun t => substitutionRate M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixedBy t (oneCopy M hM)))
      atTop (𝓝 μ)

decls.name: asexualNext
decls.doc: Fraction of asexual females in the next generation, given fraction `q` now and fecundity `f` for every female. Asexual females have `f` daughters; sexual females have `f / 2` daughters and `f / 2` sons.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def asexualNext (q f : ℝ) : ℝ := q * f / (q * f + (1 - q) * f / 2)

/-- Odds of a fraction `q`: `q / (1 - q)`. -/
noncomputable def odds (q : ℝ) : ℝ := q / (1 - q)

/-- **Twofold cost of sex.** With equal fecundity and a `1 : 1` sex ratio, the odds of asexual to
sexual females double every generation. Fecundity cancels. -/
theorem twofold_cost_of_sex {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) :
    odds (asexualNext q f) = 2 * odds q

decls.name: odds
decls.doc: Odds of a fraction `q`: `q / (1 - q)`.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def odds (q : ℝ) : ℝ := q / (1 - q)

/-- **Twofold cost of sex.** With equal fecundity and a `1 : 1` sex ratio, the odds of asexual to
sexual females double every generation. Fecundity cancels. -/
theorem twofold_cost_of_sex {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) :
    odds (asexualNext q f) = 2 * odds q

decls.name: twofold_cost_of_sex
decls.doc: **Twofold cost of sex.** With equal fecundity and a `1 : 1` sex ratio, the odds of asexual to sexual females double every generation. Fecundity cancels.
decls.statement:
theorem twofold_cost_of_sex {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) :
    odds (asexualNext q f) = 2 * odds q

decls.name: asexualNext_mem
decls.doc: The next-generation fraction stays strictly between `0` and `1`, so the identity can be iterated.
decls.statement:
theorem asexualNext_mem {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) :
    0 < asexualNext q f ∧ asexualNext q f < 1

decls.name: asexualAfter
decls.doc: Fraction of asexual females after `n` generations.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def asexualAfter (q f : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ
  | 0 => q
  | n + 1 => asexualNext (asexualAfter q f n) f

theorem asexualAfter_mem {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) (n : ℕ) :
    0 < asexualAfter q f n ∧ asexualAfter q f n < 1

decls.name: asexualAfter_mem
decls.statement:
theorem asexualAfter_mem {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) (n : ℕ) :
    0 < asexualAfter q f n ∧ asexualAfter q f n < 1

decls.name: twofold_cost_of_sex_n
decls.doc: After `n` generations the odds of asexual to sexual females are `2 ^ n` times the initial odds: an asexual lineage doubles its relative share every generation unless sex brings a compensating twofold advantage.
decls.statement:
theorem twofold_cost_of_sex_n {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) (n : ℕ) :
    odds (asexualAfter q f n) = 2 ^ n * odds q

# Two physiological laws the chain already uses: Q10 and Laplace

* **Q10.** `q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T = X0 Q10^((T - Tref)/10)`: the ratio between two temperatures is
  `Q10^((T2 - T1)/10)` and the log form has slope `log Q10 / 10` (physiology/muscle.js scales V_max, force and
  power this way with Q10 1.69, 1.08, 1.88 from Rome 1992).
* **Laplace, thin wall.** For a thin-walled sphere under transmural pressure `P`, wall stress is `P r / (2 t)`;
  for a cylinder, `P r / t` (hoop). Stress grows with radius at fixed pressure and thickness, and the pressure a
  wall of strength `σ_max` can hold falls as `1/r`: `laplace_pressure_limit`. The swim bladder and the ventral
  aorta are the chain's candidates; no wall thickness or strength is sourced for Exocoetidae, so these are
  stated-and-proved laws with no instance yet.

Named hypotheses: the Q10 form itself (an empirical rule, not a theorem of physics); thin walls (`t ≪ r`),
uniform isotropic material, static pressure.

decls.name: q10Scale
decls.doc: Temperature scaling with a Q10.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def q10Scale (X0 Q10 Tref T : ℝ) : ℝ := X0 * Q10 ^ ((T - Tref) / 10)

theorem q10_ratio {X0 Q10 Tref T₁ T₂ : ℝ} (hX : X0 ≠ 0) (hQ : 0 < Q10) :
    q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T₂ / q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T₁ = Q10 ^ ((T₂ - T₁) / 10)

decls.name: q10_ratio
decls.statement:
theorem q10_ratio {X0 Q10 Tref T₁ T₂ : ℝ} (hX : X0 ≠ 0) (hQ : 0 < Q10) :
    q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T₂ / q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T₁ = Q10 ^ ((T₂ - T₁) / 10)

decls.name: q10_log
decls.statement:
theorem q10_log {X0 Q10 Tref T₁ T₂ : ℝ} (hX : X0 ≠ 0) (hQ : 0 < Q10) :
    Real.log (q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T₂ / q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T₁) = (T₂ - T₁) / 10 * Real.log Q10

decls.name: sphereWallStress
decls.doc: Wall stress of a thin-walled sphere: `P r / (2 t)`.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def sphereWallStress (P r t : ℝ) : ℝ := P * r / (2 * t)
/-- Hoop stress of a thin-walled cylinder: `P r / t`. -/
noncomputable def hoopStress (P r t : ℝ) : ℝ := P * r / t

/-- At fixed pressure and thickness, wall stress grows with radius. -/
theorem sphereWallStress_mono {P t r₁ r₂ : ℝ} (hP : 0 < P) (ht : 0 < t) (h : r₁ ≤ r₂) :
    sphereWallStress P r₁ t ≤ sphereWallStress P r₂ t

decls.name: hoopStress
decls.doc: Hoop stress of a thin-walled cylinder: `P r / t`.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def hoopStress (P r t : ℝ) : ℝ := P * r / t

/-- At fixed pressure and thickness, wall stress grows with radius. -/
theorem sphereWallStress_mono {P t r₁ r₂ : ℝ} (hP : 0 < P) (ht : 0 < t) (h : r₁ ≤ r₂) :
    sphereWallStress P r₁ t ≤ sphereWallStress P r₂ t

decls.name: sphereWallStress_mono
decls.doc: At fixed pressure and thickness, wall stress grows with radius.
decls.statement:
theorem sphereWallStress_mono {P t r₁ r₂ : ℝ} (hP : 0 < P) (ht : 0 < t) (h : r₁ ≤ r₂) :
    sphereWallStress P r₁ t ≤ sphereWallStress P r₂ t

decls.name: laplace_pressure_limit
decls.doc: **Laplace pressure limit.** A thin spherical wall of strength `σmax` and thickness `t` holds at most `2 σmax t / r`: the pressure limit falls as `1/r`.
decls.statement:
theorem laplace_pressure_limit {P r t σmax : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (ht : 0 < t) (hσ : sphereWallStress P r t ≤ σmax) :
    P ≤ 2 * σmax * t / r

decls.name: hoop_pressure_limit
decls.statement:
theorem hoop_pressure_limit {P r t σmax : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (ht : 0 < t) (hσ : hoopStress P r t ≤ σmax) :
    P ≤ σmax * t / r

# Scaling laws of an isometric family: area, wing loading, strength, minimum speed, power (R2–R8)

Formalises the statements the physics thread handed over in `physics/FORMAL-STATEMENTS.md` (2026-10-31),
building on `CubeLaw` (R1, `Delphi/Thompson.lean`). A *family* is described by functions of one linear
dimension `L > 0`: mass `M L`, weight `W L`, lifting area `S L`, load-bearing cross-section `A L`. The laws
are **named hypotheses** on those functions, never facts about the world:

* `CubeLaw W k₁`  : `W L = k₁ L³` (isometry with constant density; R1).
* `AreaLaw S k₂`  : `S L = k₂ L²` (isometry of an area; R2).
* `MusclePowerLaw P M f p` : `P L = f p M L` with `f`, `p` constants (R6, Thompson's premise; contested).
* `σ`, `ρ`, `C_L,max`, `L/D`, `Fr` enter as constants: "the same for every member of the family".

## What is proved (every statement conditional on the named hypotheses)

* R2 `areaLaw_ratio`: `S L₂ / S L₁ = (L₂/L₁)²`.
* R3 `wingLoading_ratio`: `(W/S)(L₂) / (W/S)(L₁) = L₂/L₁`.
* R7 `breakLoad_ratio`: with `F_break = σ A`, `F_break(L₂)/F_break(L₁) = (L₂/L₁)²`; `safetyFactor_eq`:
  `F_break/W = σ k₃ / (k₁ L)`, so `stress_ratio`: `(W/A)(L₂)/(W/A)(L₁) = L₂/L₁`; `cannot_carry`: above
  `L_max = σ k₃ / (k₁ n)` the member cannot carry `n` body weights. This is the missing half of Galileo's
  square–cube argument: with R1 and R7 together, "a giant of unchanged proportions and material can stand"
  is a commitment the checker can rule on (`Delphi/Constraints.lean`, C8).
* R4 `vmin_le`: if lift `½ ρ v² S C_L` equals weight with `C_L ≤ C_L,max`, then `v ≥ √(2W/(ρ S C_L,max))`
  (exact, no isometry). `vmin_ratio`: under R1, R2 and constant `ρ`, `C_L,max`, `v_min(L₂)/v_min(L₁) = √(L₂/L₁)`.
* R5 `powerRequired_ratio`: at `v_min` with constant `L/D`, `P_req(L₂)/P_req(L₁) = (L₂/L₁)³ √(L₂/L₁)`,
  i.e. `log` exponent `7/2` (`powerRequired_log`).
* R6 `powerAvailable_ratio`: under `MusclePowerLaw` and R1, `P_avail(L₂)/P_avail(L₁) = (L₂/L₁)³`; corollary
  `exists_size_limit`: there is a size above which `P_req > P_avail` (the size exists; its value needs
  `f`, `p`, `L/D`, `ρ`, `C_L,max`, which no proof supplies).
* R8 `froude_ratio`: at equal Froude number, `v(L₂)/v(L₁) = √(L₂/L₁)`.

## What is assumed, not proved

Isometry of mass, areas and sections (real animals break it: Davenport 1992 measured fin area ∝ L^1.83 and
wing loading ∝ L^1.24 within one flying-fish species; bones thicken with size), constant density, the same
material (`σ`), the same `C_L,max` across sizes (Reynolds effects), the same `L/D`, flight at `v_min`, axial
loading, and Thompson's muscle premise (`p` constant), which modern expectation puts below `L³`. Nothing here
is a measured fact: the physics thread found one flying-fish specimen inside its own `v_min` envelope and
could not test the `(W/S)^½` scaling with the data it had. No number from `physics/results.json` appears in
any statement.

decls.name: AreaLaw
decls.doc: Isometry of an area: `S L = k L²`.
decls.statement:
def AreaLaw (S : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < k ∧ ∀ L, 0 < L → S L = k * L ^ 2

/-- Thompson's muscle premise, carried as a named hypothesis: power available is a fixed fraction `f` of
body mass times a fixed mass-specific power `p`. -/
def MusclePowerLaw (P M : ℝ → ℝ) (f p : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < f ∧ 0 < p ∧ ∀ L, 0 < L → P L = f * p * M L

lemma areaLaw_pos {S : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : AreaLaw S k) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) : 0 < S L

decls.name: MusclePowerLaw
decls.doc: Thompson's muscle premise, carried as a named hypothesis: power available is a fixed fraction `f` of body mass times a fixed mass-specific power `p`.
decls.statement:
def MusclePowerLaw (P M : ℝ → ℝ) (f p : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < f ∧ 0 < p ∧ ∀ L, 0 < L → P L = f * p * M L

lemma areaLaw_pos {S : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : AreaLaw S k) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) : 0 < S L

decls.name: areaLaw_pos
decls.statement: lemma areaLaw_pos {S : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : AreaLaw S k) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) : 0 < S L

decls.name: areaLaw_ratio
decls.doc: **R2, area law.**
decls.statement:
theorem areaLaw_ratio {S : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : AreaLaw S k) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    S L₂ / S L₁ = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 2

decls.name: wingLoading_ratio
decls.doc: **R3, wing loading.** Weight per unit area grows linearly with size.
decls.statement:
theorem wingLoading_ratio {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ}
    (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : (W L₂ / S L₂) / (W L₁ / S L₁) = L₂ / L₁

decls.name: areaLaw_log
decls.doc: The `log` form of R2: exponent `2`.
decls.statement:
theorem areaLaw_log {S : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : AreaLaw S k) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (S L₂ / S L₁) = 2 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: wingLoading_log
decls.doc: The `log` form of R3 (and of stress, below): exponent `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem wingLoading_log {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ}
    (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : Real.log ((W L₂ / S L₂) / (W L₁ / S L₁)) = 1 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: breakLoad
decls.doc: Axial breaking load of a member of cross-section `A L` made of material with breaking stress `σ`.
decls.statement:
def breakLoad (σ : ℝ) (A : ℝ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) : ℝ := σ * A L

/-- **R7, conclusion 1.** Breaking load scales as `L²`. -/
theorem breakLoad_ratio {A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₃ σ : ℝ} (hA : AreaLaw A k₃) (hσ : 0 < σ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁)
    (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : breakLoad σ A L₂ / breakLoad σ A L₁ = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 2

decls.name: breakLoad_ratio
decls.doc: **R7, conclusion 1.** Breaking load scales as `L²`.
decls.statement:
theorem breakLoad_ratio {A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₃ σ : ℝ} (hA : AreaLaw A k₃) (hσ : 0 < σ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁)
    (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : breakLoad σ A L₂ / breakLoad σ A L₁ = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 2

decls.name: safetyFactor_eq
decls.doc: **R7, conclusion 2.** The static safety factor `F_break / W` equals `σ k₃ / (k₁ L)`: it falls as `1/L`.
decls.statement:
theorem safetyFactor_eq {W A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₃ σ : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hA : AreaLaw A k₃) {L : ℝ}
    (hL : 0 < L) : breakLoad σ A L / W L = σ * k₃ / (k₁ * L)

decls.name: stress_ratio
decls.doc: **Stress grows linearly with size**: `(W/A)(L₂)/(W/A)(L₁) = L₂/L₁` (R1 with R2 on the section).
decls.statement:
theorem stress_ratio {W A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₃ : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hA : AreaLaw A k₃) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ}
    (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : (W L₂ / A L₂) / (W L₁ / A L₁) = L₂ / L₁

decls.name: safetyFactor_scaled
decls.doc: The safety factor of the body scaled by `ℓ` is the reference safety factor divided by `ℓ`.
decls.statement:
theorem safetyFactor_scaled {W A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₃ σ : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hA : AreaLaw A k₃)
    {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    breakLoad σ A L₂ / W L₂ = (breakLoad σ A L₁ / W L₁) / (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: cannot_carry
decls.doc: **Size limit.** Above `L_max = σ k₃ / (k₁ n)` the member cannot carry `n` body weights.
decls.statement:
theorem cannot_carry {W A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₃ σ n : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hA : AreaLaw A k₃) (hσ : 0 < σ)
    (hn : 0 < n) {L : ℝ} (hL : σ * k₃ / (k₁ * n) < L) : breakLoad σ A L < n * W L

decls.name: lift
decls.doc: Lift at airspeed `v`: `½ ρ v² S C_L`.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def lift (ρ v S C : ℝ) : ℝ := 1 / 2 * ρ * v ^ 2 * S * C

/-- The smallest airspeed at which lift can equal weight `W` with lifting area `S`. -/
noncomputable def vmin (ρ Cmax W S : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (2 * W / (ρ * S * Cmax))

/-- **R4, conclusion 1 (exact, no isometry).** Steady lift-supported flight at lift coefficient at most
`C_L,max` needs `v ≥ v_min`. -/
theorem vmin_le {ρ S C Cmax W v : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hS : 0 < S) (hC : 0 < C) (hCmax : C ≤ Cmax) (hv : 0 ≤ v)
    (hlift : lift ρ v S C = W) : vmin ρ Cmax W S ≤ v

decls.name: vmin
decls.doc: The smallest airspeed at which lift can equal weight `W` with lifting area `S`.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def vmin (ρ Cmax W S : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (2 * W / (ρ * S * Cmax))

/-- **R4, conclusion 1 (exact, no isometry).** Steady lift-supported flight at lift coefficient at most
`C_L,max` needs `v ≥ v_min`. -/
theorem vmin_le {ρ S C Cmax W v : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hS : 0 < S) (hC : 0 < C) (hCmax : C ≤ Cmax) (hv : 0 ≤ v)
    (hlift : lift ρ v S C = W) : vmin ρ Cmax W S ≤ v

decls.name: vmin_le
decls.doc: **R4, conclusion 1 (exact, no isometry).** Steady lift-supported flight at lift coefficient at most `C_L,max` needs `v ≥ v_min`.
decls.statement:
theorem vmin_le {ρ S C Cmax W v : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hS : 0 < S) (hC : 0 < C) (hCmax : C ≤ Cmax) (hv : 0 ≤ v)
    (hlift : lift ρ v S C = W) : vmin ρ Cmax W S ≤ v

decls.name: vmin_ratio
decls.doc: **R4, conclusion 2.** Under R1, R2 and the same `ρ`, `C_L,max` for every member, `v_min` scales as `√L`.
decls.statement:
theorem vmin_ratio {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) (hρ : 0 < ρ)
    (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂) / vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁) = Real.sqrt (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: vmin_log
decls.doc: The `log` form of R4: exponent `1/2`.
decls.statement:
theorem vmin_log {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) (hρ : 0 < ρ)
    (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂) / vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁)) = 1 / 2 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: powerRequired
decls.doc: Mechanical power to sustain level flight at speed `v`: thrust equals drag, `P = W v / (L/D)`.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def powerRequired (W v LD : ℝ) : ℝ := W * v / LD

/-- **R5.** At `v_min`, with constant `L/D`, power required scales as `L³ √L`, i.e. `L^3.5`. -/
theorem powerRequired_ratio {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax LD : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂)
    (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) (hLD : 0 < LD) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    powerRequired (W L₂) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂)) LD / powerRequired (W L₁) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁)) LD
      = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 3 * Real.sqrt (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: powerRequired_ratio
decls.doc: **R5.** At `v_min`, with constant `L/D`, power required scales as `L³ √L`, i.e. `L^3.5`.
decls.statement:
theorem powerRequired_ratio {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax LD : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂)
    (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) (hLD : 0 < LD) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    powerRequired (W L₂) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂)) LD / powerRequired (W L₁) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁)) LD
      = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 3 * Real.sqrt (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: powerRequired_log
decls.doc: The `log` form of R5: exponent `7/2`.
decls.statement:
theorem powerRequired_log {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax LD : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂)
    (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) (hLD : 0 < LD) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (powerRequired (W L₂) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂)) LD /
      powerRequired (W L₁) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁)) LD) = 7 / 2 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: powerAvailable_ratio
decls.doc: **R6 (as a named hypothesis).** Under Thompson's muscle premise and R1, power available scales as `L³`.
decls.statement:
theorem powerAvailable_ratio {P M : ℝ → ℝ} {f p k : ℝ} (hP : MusclePowerLaw P M f p) (hM : CubeLaw M k)
    {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : P L₂ / P L₁ = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 3

decls.name: powerRatio_eq
decls.doc: The ratio `P_req / P_avail` equals `c √L` for an explicit positive constant `c`.
decls.statement:
theorem powerRatio_eq {W S M P : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ kM ρ Cmax LD f p : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂)
    (hM : CubeLaw M kM) (hP : MusclePowerLaw P M f p) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) (hLD : 0 < LD)
    {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) :
    powerRequired (W L) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L) (S L)) LD / P L
      = k₁ / (LD * f * p * kM) * Real.sqrt (2 * k₁ / (ρ * k₂ * Cmax)) * Real.sqrt L

decls.name: exists_size_limit
decls.doc: **Corollary of R5 and R6 (Thompson's "a bird as large as a man could not fly").** There is a size above which the power required exceeds the power available. The size exists; its value is not supplied.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_size_limit {W S M P : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ kM ρ Cmax LD f p : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁)
    (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) (hM : CubeLaw M kM) (hP : MusclePowerLaw P M f p) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax)
    (hLD : 0 < LD) : ∃ Ls : ℝ, 0 < Ls ∧ ∀ L, Ls < L → P L < powerRequired (W L) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L) (S L)) LD

decls.name: SectionModulusLaw
decls.doc: Geometrically similar sections: the section modulus is `k L³` (`Z = k_Z d³` with `d = k_d L`).
decls.statement:
def SectionModulusLaw (Z : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < k ∧ ∀ L, 0 < L → Z L = k * L ^ 3

/-- The lever arm scales with the body: `ℓ = k L`. -/
def LeverLaw (ℓ : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < k ∧ ∀ L, 0 < L → ℓ L = k * L

/-- Maximum bending stress of a slender linear-elastic beam under transverse load `F` at lever arm `ℓ`:
`σ_b = M_b / Z = F ℓ / Z`. -/
noncomputable def bendingStress (F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) : ℝ := F L * ℓ L / Z L

/-- **R9a, conclusion 1 (body-like load).** With the load scaling as the body (`CubeLaw F`), lever arm `∝ L` and
similar sections (`Z ∝ L³`), bending stress scales as `L`. -/
theorem bendingStress_ratio_body {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)

decls.name: LeverLaw
decls.doc: The lever arm scales with the body: `ℓ = k L`.
decls.statement:
def LeverLaw (ℓ : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < k ∧ ∀ L, 0 < L → ℓ L = k * L

/-- Maximum bending stress of a slender linear-elastic beam under transverse load `F` at lever arm `ℓ`:
`σ_b = M_b / Z = F ℓ / Z`. -/
noncomputable def bendingStress (F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) : ℝ := F L * ℓ L / Z L

/-- **R9a, conclusion 1 (body-like load).** With the load scaling as the body (`CubeLaw F`), lever arm `∝ L` and
similar sections (`Z ∝ L³`), bending stress scales as `L`. -/
theorem bendingStress_ratio_body {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁ = L₂ / L₁

decls.name: bendingStress
decls.doc: Maximum bending stress of a slender linear-elastic beam under transverse load `F` at lever arm `ℓ`: `σ_b = M_b / Z = F ℓ / Z`.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def bendingStress (F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) : ℝ := F L * ℓ L / Z L

/-- **R9a, conclusion 1 (body-like load).** With the load scaling as the body (`CubeLaw F`), lever arm `∝ L` and
similar sections (`Z ∝ L³`), bending stress scales as `L`. -/
theorem bendingStress_ratio_body {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁ = L₂ / L₁

decls.name: bendingStress_ratio_body
decls.doc: **R9a, conclusion 1 (body-like load).** With the load scaling as the body (`CubeLaw F`), lever arm `∝ L` and similar sections (`Z ∝ L³`), bending stress scales as `L`.
decls.statement:
theorem bendingStress_ratio_body {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁ = L₂ / L₁

decls.name: bendingStress_log_body
decls.doc: The `log` form of R9a: exponent `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem bendingStress_log_body {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁) = 1 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: bendingSafety_eq
decls.doc: **R9a, conclusion 2.** The bending safety factor `σ_max / σ_b` equals `σ_max k_Z / (k_F k_ℓ L)`: it falls as `1/L`.
decls.statement:
theorem bendingSafety_eq {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ σmax : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) :
    σmax / bendingStress F ℓ Z L = σmax * kZ / (kF * kℓ * L)

decls.name: bending_cannot_carry
decls.doc: **Size limit in bending.** Above `L_max,b = σ_max k_Z / (k_F k_ℓ n)` the member cannot carry `n` times its load in bending: the stress at `n` times the load exceeds `σ_max`. Same shape as `cannot_carry`.

decls.name: bendingStress_ratio_sheet
decls.doc: **R9b (sheet-like load).** If the load scales as an area (`AreaLaw F`, a lamina of constant thickness), bending stress is independent of size: no size limit follows.
decls.statement:
theorem bendingStress_ratio_sheet {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : AreaLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁ = 1

decls.name: bendingStress_log_sheet
decls.doc: The `log` form of R9b: exponent `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem bendingStress_log_sheet {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : AreaLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁) = 0 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: froudeSpeed
decls.doc: Speed at a fixed Froude number `Fr = v² / (g L)`.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def froudeSpeed (Fr g L : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (Fr * g * L)

/-- **R8.** At equal Froude number, speed scales as `√L`. -/
theorem froude_ratio {Fr g : ℝ} (hFr : 0 < Fr) (hg : 0 < g) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    froudeSpeed Fr g L₂ / froudeSpeed Fr g L₁ = Real.sqrt (L₂ / L₁)

decls.name: froude_ratio
decls.doc: **R8.** At equal Froude number, speed scales as `√L`.
decls.statement:
theorem froude_ratio {Fr g : ℝ} (hFr : 0 < Fr) (hg : 0 < g) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    froudeSpeed Fr g L₂ / froudeSpeed Fr g L₁ = Real.sqrt (L₂ / L₁)

modules.header:
# Thompson (1917): weight varies as the cube of a linear dimension

Claim `thompson1917-ch03-07` (On Growth and Form, chapter III): during growth, weight tends to vary
as the cube of a linear dimension, so the weight curve is approximately the cube of the stature curve.

## What is proved

* `CubeLaw W k`: a family of bodies of linear size `L` whose weight is `W L = k L^3` with `k > 0`
  (isometric growth at constant density: the shape and the density do not change, so weight is
  proportional to volume and volume to the cube of any linear dimension).
* `cubeLaw_loglog_exponent`: for any two sizes `L₁ ≠ L₂` the log-log slope
  `(log W L₂ - log W L₁) / (log L₂ - log L₁)` equals exactly `3`. This is the quantity the claim test
  measures (`claim-tests/thompson-growth-form/thompson1917-ch03-07`).
* `cubeLaw_ratio`: equivalently `W L₂ / W L₁ = (L₂ / L₁)^3`.
* `not_cubeLaw_of_exponent_ne_three`: the contrapositive the data test uses. If two measured sizes
  give a log-log slope different from `3`, then no `k` makes the family a cube law: the growth is not
  isometric at constant density on that interval.

## What is assumed, not proved

* "Linear dimension" and "weight" are read as a single length `L` and mass `W` of the same body family;
  density constant and shape fixed are what `W = k L^3` encodes. Thompson's "mainly (though not wholly)"
  is not formalised: the theorem is exact, the law is approximate, and the tolerance band
  `[2.5, 3.5]` used by the claim test is a decision rule outside this module.
* Nothing about any dataset: the measured exponents (NHANES age-bin means, claims thread) live in the
  claim test's result files and are pointed to from the record, not derived here.

decls.name: CubeLaw
decls.doc: Isometric growth at constant density: weight is `k` times the cube of the linear dimension.
decls.statement:
def CubeLaw (W : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < k ∧ ∀ L, 0 < L → W L = k * L ^ 3

/-- The log-log slope between two sizes. -/
noncomputable def logSlope (W : ℝ → ℝ) (L₁ L₂ : ℝ) : ℝ := (log (W L₂) - log (W L₁)) / (log L₂ - log L₁)

lemma cubeLaw_pos {W : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : CubeLaw W k) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) : 0 < W L

decls.name: logSlope
decls.doc: The log-log slope between two sizes.
decls.statement:
noncomputable def logSlope (W : ℝ → ℝ) (L₁ L₂ : ℝ) : ℝ := (log (W L₂) - log (W L₁)) / (log L₂ - log L₁)

lemma cubeLaw_pos {W : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : CubeLaw W k) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) : 0 < W L

decls.name: cubeLaw_pos
decls.statement: lemma cubeLaw_pos {W : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : CubeLaw W k) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) : 0 < W L

decls.name: cubeLaw_ratio
decls.doc: **Weight ratio is the cube of the size ratio.**
decls.statement:
theorem cubeLaw_ratio {W : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : CubeLaw W k) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    W L₂ / W L₁ = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 3

decls.name: cubeLaw_loglog_exponent
decls.doc: **The log-log exponent of a cube law is exactly 3.**
decls.statement:
theorem cubeLaw_loglog_exponent {W : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : CubeLaw W k) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁)
    (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂) : logSlope W L₁ L₂ = 3

decls.name: not_cubeLaw_of_exponent_ne_three
decls.doc: **What a measured exponent other than 3 refutes.** If two sizes give a log-log slope `b ≠ 3`, the family is not a cube law for any constant `k`.
decls.statement:
theorem not_cubeLaw_of_exponent_ne_three {W : ℝ → ℝ} {L₁ L₂ b : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂)
    (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂) (hb : logSlope W L₁ L₂ = b) (hb3 : b ≠ 3) : ∀ k, ¬ CubeLaw W k

theorems.name: vmin_mono
theorems.doc: **The minimum speed rises with height.**
theorems.statement:
theorem vmin_mono {W S CL : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hS : 0 < S) (hCL : 0 < CL) {h₁ h₂ : ℝ} (h : h₁ ≤ h₂) :
    vminAt A W S CL h₁ ≤ vminAt A W S CL h₂

theorems.name: demand_mono
theorems.doc: **The power required rises with height**, because the minimum speed does.
theorems.statement:
theorem demand_mono {W S CL LD : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hS : 0 < S) (hCL : 0 < CL) (hLD : 0 < LD)
    {h₁ h₂ : ℝ} (h : h₁ ≤ h₂) : demandAt A W S CL LD h₁ ≤ demandAt A W S CL LD h₂

theorems.name: supply_anti
theorems.doc: **The aerobic supply falls with height**, because the oxygen partial pressure does and arterial content is nondecreasing in it.

theorems.name: feasible_downward_closed
theorems.doc: **The feasible heights reach down to the ground.** If the design can fly at a height, it can fly at every lower one: demand only falls as you descend and supply only rises.
theorems.statement:
theorem feasible_downward_closed {ca : ℝ → ℝ} (hca : ∀ x y : ℝ, x ≤ y → ca x ≤ ca y)
    {W S CL LD eta E Q : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hS : 0 < S) (hCL : 0 < CL) (hLD : 0 < LD)
    (he : 0 ≤ eta) (hE : 0 ≤ E) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) {h₁ h₂ : ℝ} (hle : h₁ ≤ h₂)
    (hfeas : Feasible A ca W S CL LD eta E Q h₂) : Feasible A ca W S CL LD eta E Q h₁

theorems.name: ceiling
theorems.doc: **A ceiling exists**, in the only sense this model can give one: above an infeasible height, every height is infeasible. The feasible set is therefore an interval from the ground up to a ceiling, which may be empty (nothing says the ground itself is feasible) and whose value this theorem does not compute.
theorems.statement:
theorem ceiling {ca : ℝ → ℝ} (hca : ∀ x y : ℝ, x ≤ y → ca x ≤ ca y)
    {W S CL LD eta E Q : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hS : 0 < S) (hCL : 0 < CL) (hLD : 0 < LD)
    (he : 0 ≤ eta) (hE : 0 ≤ E) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) {h₀ : ℝ} (hinf : ¬ Feasible A ca W S CL LD eta E Q h₀) :
    ∀ h, h₀ ≤ h → ¬ Feasible A ca W S CL LD eta E Q h

theorems.name: infeasible_at_ground_infeasible_everywhere
theorems.doc: **What matters for the flying fish.** A design whose oxygen budget cannot pay for flight at the ground cannot pay for it at any height, so altitude explains nothing about such a design. The real fish is in this case at sea level by a factor of about thirty (C14), and the gentle shrink of the feasible region with height is NOT the reason.
theorems.statement:
theorem infeasible_at_ground_infeasible_everywhere {ca : ℝ → ℝ} (hca : ∀ x y : ℝ, x ≤ y → ca x ≤ ca y)
    {W S CL LD eta E Q : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hS : 0 < S) (hCL : 0 < CL) (hLD : 0 < LD)
    (he : 0 ≤ eta) (hE : 0 ≤ E) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hground : ¬ Feasible A ca W S CL LD eta E Q 0) :
    ∀ h, 0 ≤ h → ¬ Feasible A ca W S CL LD eta E Q h

theorems.name: demand_anti_area
theorems.doc: **The wing can be traded against the oxygen budget, but only at a fixed height.** A larger lifting area lowers the minimum speed and so the power required; this says nothing about altitude, and it is the only direction in which the two sides of the constraint can be exchanged.
theorems.statement:
theorem demand_anti_area {W CL LD h : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hCL : 0 < CL) (hLD : 0 < LD)
    {S₁ S₂ : ℝ} (hS₁ : 0 < S₁) (hS : S₁ ≤ S₂) :
    demandAt A W S₂ CL LD h ≤ demandAt A W S₁ CL LD h

theorems.name: Graph.transGen_trans
theorems.doc: The transitive closure is transitive: `X part_of* Y → Y part_of* Z → X part_of* Z`.
theorems.statement:
theorem Graph.transGen_trans (g : Graph α) {a b c : α} (h₁ : g.PartOfStar a b) (h₂ : g.PartOfStar b c) :
    g.PartOfStar a c

theorems.name: Graph.partOfStar_of_edge
theorems.doc: A stated edge is in the closure.
theorems.statement: theorem Graph.partOfStar_of_edge (g : Graph α) {a b : α} (h : g.Edge a b) : g.PartOfStar a b

theorems.name: Graph.transGen_level_lt
theorems.doc: Along the closure the level strictly decreases.
theorems.statement:
theorem Graph.transGen_level_lt (g : Graph α) (hL : g.LevelsDown) {a b : α} (h : g.PartOfStar a b) :
    g.level b < g.level a

theorems.name: Graph.acyclic_of_levelsDown
theorems.doc: **Acyclicity.** If every edge goes strictly down in level, nothing is part of itself.
theorems.statement: theorem Graph.acyclic_of_levelsDown (g : Graph α) (hL : g.LevelsDown) : g.Acyclic

theorems.name: Graph.rooted_of
theorems.doc: **No orphans.** If edges go strictly down, every edge's whole is a node, and every non-root node has a whole, then every node reaches the root. Strong induction on the level.
theorems.statement:
theorem Graph.rooted_of (g : Graph α) (hL : g.LevelsDown) (hC : ∀ e ∈ g.partOf, e.2 ∈ g.nodes)
    (hP : ∀ a ∈ g.nodes, a ≠ g.root → ∃ b, g.Edge a b) : g.Rooted

theorems.name: Graph.levelsDown_of_check
theorems.statement: theorem Graph.levelsDown_of_check (g : Graph α) (h : g.levelsDownB = true) : g.LevelsDown

theorems.name: Graph.closed_of_check
theorems.statement: theorem Graph.closed_of_check (g : Graph α) (h : g.closedB = true) : g.Closed

theorems.name: Graph.hasParent_of_check
theorems.statement: theorem Graph.hasParent_of_check (g : Graph α) (a : α) (h : g.hasParentB a = true) : ∃ b, g.Edge a b

theorems.name: Graph.rooted_of_check
theorems.statement:
theorem Graph.rooted_of_check (g : Graph α) (hL : g.levelsDownB = true) (hC : g.closedB = true)
    (hR : g.rootedB = true) : g.Rooted

theorems.name: TaxonData.ok_of_check
theorems.statement: theorem TaxonData.ok_of_check (D : TaxonData α τ) (h : D.okB = true) : D.Ok

theorems.name: wellFormed_of_check
theorems.doc: **Soundness of the checker.** If `check g D` evaluates to `true`, the graph is well-formed.
theorems.statement: theorem wellFormed_of_check (g : Graph α) (D : TaxonData α τ) (h : check g D = true) : WellFormed g D

theorems.name: ne_of_lt_intervals
theorems.doc: Two quantities confined to disjoint intervals are unequal.
theorems.statement:
theorem ne_of_lt_intervals {x y a b c d : ℝ} (hx : a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ b) (hy : c ≤ y ∧ y ≤ d) (h : b < c) :
    x ≠ y

theorems.name: kimura_rate_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C1, Kimura's rate.** A candidate that commits the neutral substitution rate to `[a, b]` and the mutation rate to `[c, d]`, with the intervals disjoint, is ruled out: the rate equals `μ`.
theorems.statement:
theorem kimura_rate_rules_out (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) {a b c d : ℝ}
    (hk : a ≤ substitutionRate M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) ∧
      substitutionRate M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) ≤ b)
    (hμ : c ≤ μ ∧ μ ≤ d) (h : b < c ∨ d < a) : False

theorems.name: kimura_rate_ratio_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C1b, Kimura's rate between lineages.** Two neutral lineages with the same mutation rate cannot have substitution rates in a ratio other than `1`: a candidate that commits to equal mutation rates and an `r`-fold difference in neutral substitution rate (for example "caused by population size") is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem kimura_rate_ratio_rules_out (M₁ M₂ : ℕ) (h₁ : 0 < M₁) (h₂ : 0 < M₂) (μ₁ μ₂ r : ℝ)
    (hμ : μ₁ = μ₂) (hpos : 0 < μ₁)
    (hk : substitutionRate M₂ μ₂ ((wrightFisher M₂ h₂).fixationProbability (oneCopy M₂ h₂)) =
      r * substitutionRate M₁ μ₁ ((wrightFisher M₁ h₁).fixationProbability (oneCopy M₁ h₁)))
    (hr : r ≠ 1) : False

theorems.name: neutral_fixation_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C2, neutral fixation.** A candidate that confines the fixation probability of one new neutral mutant among `M` copies to an interval not containing `1/M` is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem neutral_fixation_rules_out (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) {a b : ℝ}
    (hu : a ≤ (wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM) ∧
      (wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM) ≤ b)
    (h : b < 1 / (M : ℝ) ∨ 1 / (M : ℝ) < a) : False

theorems.name: favored_fixation_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C3, the favored floor.** A candidate that says a mutant selection does not oppose (`s ≥ 0`) fixes with probability at most `b < 1/M` is ruled out.

theorems.name: supply_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C3b, the supply ceiling.** A candidate that commits to an expected number of substitutions over `G` sites and `T` generations above the mutation supply `G · M · μ · T` is ruled out, for any fixation probability `u ≤ 1`. (An expectation, not a realised count.)
theorems.statement:
theorem supply_rules_out (M : ℕ) (μ u : ℝ) (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hu : u ≤ 1) (T : ℕ) {G c : ℝ} (hG : 0 ≤ G)
    (hc : c = G * expectedSubstitutions M μ u T) (h : G * ((M : ℝ) * μ * T) < c) : False

theorems.name: supply_rules_out'
theorems.doc: **C3b, interval form.** The mutation rate at most `μh` and the committed expectation at least `cl`: ruled out when `G · M · μh · T < cl`.
theorems.statement:
theorem supply_rules_out' (M : ℕ) (μ u : ℝ) (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hu : u ≤ 1) (T : ℕ) {G cl μh : ℝ} (hG : 0 ≤ G)
    (hμh : μ ≤ μh) (hc : cl ≤ G * expectedSubstitutions M μ u T) (h : G * ((M : ℝ) * μh * T) < cl) :
    False

theorems.name: fisher_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C4, Fisher.** A candidate that commits to a change in mean fitness `Δ`, a mean fitness `m > 0` and a variance in fitness `V` under one round of selection with fixed fitnesses, with `Δ · m ≠ V`, is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem fisher_rules_out {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {p w : ι → ℝ} (hp : IsFreq p)
    (hmean : 0 < meanFitness p w) {Δ V m : ℝ}
    (hΔ : meanFitness (select p w) w - meanFitness p w = Δ) (hV : variance p w = V)
    (hm : meanFitness p w = m) (h : Δ * m ≠ V) : False

theorems.name: fisher_decline_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C4b, Fisher's sign.** A candidate that says mean fitness falls under one round of selection with fixed fitnesses is ruled out.

theorems.name: fisher_zero_variance_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C4c, Fisher with zero variance.** If the variance in fitness is `0`, mean fitness does not change at all: a candidate that commits to zero variance and a nonzero change is ruled out.

theorems.name: twofold_factor_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C5b, the per-generation factor.** Under equal fecundity and a 1:1 sex ratio the odds of asexual females grow by exactly `2` per generation: a candidate committing to any other factor is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem twofold_factor_rules_out {q f r : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f)
    (hr : odds (asexualNext q f) = r * odds q) (h : r ≠ 2) : False

theorems.name: twofold_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C5, the twofold cost.** A candidate that commits the asexual fraction to `q` now and `qn` after `n` generations, under equal fecundity and a 1:1 sex ratio, with `odds qn ≠ 2^n · odds q`, is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem twofold_rules_out {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) (n : ℕ) {qn : ℝ}
    (hqn : asexualAfter q f n = qn) (h : odds qn ≠ 2 ^ n * odds q) : False

theorems.name: cubeLaw_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C7, the cube law.** A candidate that commits to isometric scaling at constant density from size `L₁` to `L₂` with length ratio `ℓ` and weight ratio `r ≠ ℓ^3` is ruled out. (Only the mass side of Galileo's square–cube argument: strength scaling as `L^2` is not formalised.)
theorems.statement:
theorem cubeLaw_rules_out {W : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : CubeLaw W k) {L₁ L₂ r ℓ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁)
    (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hr : W L₂ / W L₁ = r) (hℓ : L₂ / L₁ = ℓ) (hne : r ≠ ℓ ^ 3) : False

theorems.name: cubeLaw_rules_out'
theorems.doc: **C7, interval form.** Weight ratio confined to `[a, b]` and length ratio to `[c, d]` with `0 ≤ c`: ruled out when `[a, b]` and `[c^3, d^3]` are disjoint.
theorems.statement:
theorem cubeLaw_rules_out' {W : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : CubeLaw W k) {L₁ L₂ a b c d : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁)
    (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hr : a ≤ W L₂ / W L₁ ∧ W L₂ / W L₁ ≤ b) (hℓ : c ≤ L₂ / L₁ ∧ L₂ / L₁ ≤ d)
    (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hne : b < c ^ 3 ∨ d ^ 3 < a) : False

theorems.name: exponent_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C7b, the exponent form.** A log-log exponent confined to an interval not containing `3`, under isometric scaling at constant density, is ruled out for every `k`.
theorems.statement:
theorem exponent_rules_out {W : ℝ → ℝ} {L₁ L₂ a b : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂)
    (hb : a ≤ logSlope W L₁ L₂ ∧ logSlope W L₁ L₂ ≤ b) (h : b < 3 ∨ 3 < a) : ∀ k, ¬ CubeLaw W k

theorems.name: axial_strength_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C8, axial strength, dimensional.** A member of cross-section `A` and breaking stress `σ` that is claimed to carry `n` body weights `W` is ruled out when `σ A < n W`.
theorems.statement:
theorem axial_strength_rules_out {σ A W n F : ℝ} (hF : F = σ * A) (hclaim : n * W ≤ F) (h : σ * A < n * W) :
    False

theorems.name: strength_ratio_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C8b, strength scaling.** Under isometric sections and the same material, breaking load scales as `L²`: a committed breaking-load ratio `r` at length ratio `ℓ` with `r ≠ ℓ²` is ruled out.

theorems.name: giant_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C8c, Galileo's giant.** A body scaled by `ℓ` with unchanged proportions and material, whose reference member carries `n₀` body weights, is claimed to carry `n` body weights: ruled out when `n₀ < n ℓ`.

theorems.name: stress_ratio_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C8d, stress scaling.** Under R1 and isometric sections, stress `W/A` grows as `L`: a committed stress ratio `r` at length ratio `ℓ` with `r ≠ ℓ` is ruled out.

theorems.name: area_ratio_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C2a, area scaling.** Under isometry an area scales as `L²`: a committed area ratio `r` at length ratio `ℓ` with `r ≠ ℓ²` is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem area_ratio_rules_out {S : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (hS : AreaLaw S k) {L₁ L₂ r ℓ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂)
    (hr : S L₂ / S L₁ = r) (hℓ : L₂ / L₁ = ℓ) (hne : r ≠ ℓ ^ 2) : False

theorems.name: area_exponent_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C2a, area exponent.** Under isometry an area's log-log exponent on `L` is `2`.
theorems.statement:
theorem area_exponent_rules_out {S : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (hS : AreaLaw S k) {L₁ L₂ b : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂)
    (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂) (hb : Real.log (S L₂ / S L₁) = b * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)) (h : b ≠ 2) : False

theorems.name: stress_exponent_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C8e, stress (or wing-loading) exponent.** Under R1 and isometric areas the exponent of `W/A` on `L` is `1`.

theorems.name: vmin_exponent_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C9c, minimum-speed exponent.** Under R1, R2 and constant `ρ`, `C_L,max`, the exponent of `v_min` on `L` is `1/2`.
theorems.statement:
theorem vmin_exponent_rules_out {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂)
    (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) {L₁ L₂ b : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂)
    (hb : Real.log (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂) / vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁)) = b * Real.log (L₂ / L₁))
    (h : b ≠ 1 / 2) : False

theorems.name: vmin_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C9, minimum speed.** Steady lift-supported flight at airspeed `v` with `v² < 2W/(ρ S C_L,max)` is ruled out (`v < v_min`).
theorems.statement:
theorem vmin_rules_out {ρ S C Cmax W v : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hS : 0 < S) (hC : 0 < C) (hCmax : C ≤ Cmax)
    (hv : 0 ≤ v) (hlift : lift ρ v S C = W) (h : v ^ 2 < 2 * W / (ρ * S * Cmax)) : False

theorems.name: vmin_scaling_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C9b, minimum-speed scaling.** Under R1, R2 and constant `ρ`, `C_L,max`, `v_min` scales as `√L`: a committed `v_min` ratio `r ≥ 0` at length ratio `ℓ` with `r² ≠ ℓ` is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem vmin_scaling_rules_out {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂)
    (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) {L₁ L₂ r ℓ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂)
    (hr : vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂) / vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁) = r) (hℓ : L₂ / L₁ = ℓ) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r)
    (hne : r ^ 2 ≠ ℓ) : False

theorems.name: powerRequired_exponent_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C10, power required.** Under R1, R2, constant `ρ`, `C_L,max` and `L/D`, flight at `v_min`: a committed log-log exponent `b ≠ 7/2` of `P_req` on `L` is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem powerRequired_exponent_rules_out {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax LD : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁)
    (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) (hLD : 0 < LD) {L₁ L₂ b : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂)
    (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂)
    (hb : Real.log (powerRequired (W L₂) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂)) LD /
      powerRequired (W L₁) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁)) LD) = b * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)) (h : b ≠ 7 / 2) : False

theorems.name: bending_exponent_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C12, bending exponent, body-like load.** Under R9a the exponent of bending stress on `L` is `1`.
theorems.statement:
theorem bending_exponent_rules_out {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ b : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂)
    (hb : Real.log (bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁) = b * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)) (h : b ≠ 1) :
    False

theorems.name: bending_ratio_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C12b, bending ratio, body-like load.** A committed bending-stress ratio `r ≠ ℓ` is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem bending_ratio_rules_out {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ r q : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂)
    (hr : bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁ = r) (hq : L₂ / L₁ = q) (hne : r ≠ q) : False

theorems.name: bending_exponent_sheet_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C12c, bending exponent, sheet-like load.** Under R9b the exponent is `0`: a candidate with a constant-thickness lamina that still commits to bending stress rising (or falling) with size is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem bending_exponent_sheet_rules_out {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : AreaLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ b : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂)
    (hb : Real.log (bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁) = b * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)) (h : b ≠ 0) :
    False

theorems.name: allometry_consistency_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C13, allometric consistency.** If weight and lifting area are power laws with exponents `bW`, `bS`, the wing-loading exponent is `bW - bS`: a committed triple with `bWS ≠ bW - bS` is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem allometry_consistency_rules_out {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {aW bW aS bS bWS : ℝ} (hW : PowerLaw W aW bW)
    (hS : PowerLaw S aS bS) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂)
    (hb : Real.log ((W L₂ / S L₂) / (W L₁ / S L₁)) = bWS * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)) (h : bWS ≠ bW - bS) : False

theorems.name: aerobic_flight_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C14, aerobic sustained flight.** A claim of sustained (aerobic) flight at power `P_req = W v/(L/D)` with `η E Q Ca < P_req` is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem aerobic_flight_rules_out {W v LD P η E Q Ca Cv : ℝ} (hη : 0 ≤ η) (hE : 0 ≤ E) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hCv : 0 ≤ Cv)
    (hsus : P ≤ aerobicPower η E Q Ca Cv) (hflight : powerRequired W v LD ≤ P)
    (h : η * E * Q * Ca < powerRequired W v LD) : False

theorems.name: glide_range_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C15, glide range.** A claimed steady unpowered glide of distance `x > h (L/D)_max / (1 - δ)` from height `h` with drag reduced by a fraction `δ` near the surface (`δ = 0` away from it) is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem glide_range_rules_out {W h D x LDmax loss Lift δ : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hD : 0 < D) (hh : 0 ≤ h)
    (hδ0 : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ1 : δ < 1) (hlift : Lift = W) (hLD : Lift / D ≤ LDmax)
    (henergy : W * h = (1 - δ) * D * x + loss) (hloss : 0 ≤ loss) (hx : h * LDmax / (1 - δ) < x) : False

theorems.name: climb_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C16, climb.** A claimed climb rate `c` above `(P_avail - P_req)/W` under the power balance is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem climb_rules_out {W Pavail Preq c loss : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hbal : Pavail = Preq + W * c + loss)
    (hloss : 0 ≤ loss) (h : climbRate W Pavail Preq < c) : False

theorems.name: froude_rules_out
theorems.doc: **C11, Froude.** At equal Froude number speed scales as `√L`: a committed speed ratio `r ≥ 0` at length ratio `ℓ` with `r² ≠ ℓ` is ruled out.
theorems.statement:
theorem froude_rules_out {Fr g : ℝ} (hFr : 0 < Fr) (hg : 0 < g) {L₁ L₂ r ℓ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂)
    (hr : froudeSpeed Fr g L₂ / froudeSpeed Fr g L₁ = r) (hℓ : L₂ / L₁ = ℓ) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hne : r ^ 2 ≠ ℓ) :
    False

theorems.name: not_isometric_area
theorems.doc: **The area law fails** under this observation: the exponent is not 2, so `AreaLaw` cannot hold with it.
theorems.statement: theorem not_isometric_area (A : WithinSpeciesAllometry) : A.areaExponent ≠ 2

theorems.name: loading_rises
theorems.doc: **Wing loading rises with size** under this observation: a bigger member of the family is more loaded, which is the content of the measured 1.236 rather than the isometric 1.

theorems.name: weight_ratio_band
theorems.doc: **A scaled design's weight ratio must lie in the measured band.** For a weight that follows one power law over the range, the ratio between two lengths is between `r^2.90` and `r^3.02`.

theorems.name: weight_ratio_rules_out
theorems.doc: A design committing a weight ratio outside the band, under one power law, is ruled out.

theorems.name: aerobicCeiling_le
theorems.doc: **The aerobic ceiling of anything inside the measured ranges is at most 0.0458 W.** This is what makes the C14 eliminations binding rather than a choice of proxies: no teleost the measured record allows, at this mass, has a larger sustained aerobic ceiling.
theorems.statement:
theorem aerobicCeiling_le (T : TeleostAerobic) :
    T.eta * T.oxycaloric * T.cardiacOutput * T.arterialO2 ≤ 0.0458

theorems.name: no_aerobic_flight_above_ceiling
theorems.doc: **No teleost inside the measured ranges can fly aerobically above that ceiling.** Composed with the Fick bound of lean/Delphi/Flight.lean: a sustained flight needing more than 0.0458 W is ruled out for every animal the measured record allows, not only for one set of proxies.
theorems.statement:
theorem no_aerobic_flight_above_ceiling (T : TeleostAerobic) {W v LD P Cv : ℝ} (hCv : 0 ≤ Cv)
    (hsus : P ≤ aerobicPower T.eta T.oxycaloric T.cardiacOutput T.arterialO2 Cv)
    (hflight : powerRequired W v LD ≤ P) (hbig : 0.0458 < powerRequired W v LD) : False

theorems.name: stored_power_le
theorems.doc: **Airborne aerobic power is time-limited.** With no uptake, a flight of duration `t > 0` can spend at most the store `S` (ml O2) at `E` J/ml, so the mean mechanical power is at most `E S / t`. Nothing here bounds anaerobic (burst) power, which is what a flying fish is understood to use.
theorems.statement:
theorem stored_power_le (_U : NoAerialUptake) {Eo2 S t P : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t)
    (hspend : P * t ≤ Eo2 * S) : P ≤ Eo2 * S / t

theorems.name: finRatio_outside
theorems.doc: A ratio outside the measured range is above or below it: a statement about the record, not about what is possible. No theorem here says such a fish cannot exist.
theorems.statement: theorem finRatio_outside {r : ℝ} (h : ¬ measuredFinRatio r) : r < 0.406 ∨ 0.823 < r

theorems.name: requiredFor_not_propagated_of_check
theorems.doc: Soundness of the check: if it passes, no "required for" row was derived by downward propagation.

theorems.name: requiredFor_propagated_violates
theorems.doc: A row that breaks the convention makes the check fail.

theorems.name: cannot_score_of_lethal_before
theorems.doc: **An intervention lethal at or before the scoring stage cannot produce the scored phenotype.**
theorems.statement: theorem cannot_score_of_lethal_before {d s : ℕ} (h : d ≤ s) : ¬ CanScore d s

theorems.name: empirical_nonvacuous
theorems.doc: **The empirical layer is non-vacuous**: the measured numbers satisfy every entry at once.
theorems.statement:
theorem empirical_nonvacuous : Nonempty Record := ⟨measured⟩

/-- The measured aerobic proxies are inside the measured ranges, so the ceiling theorem applies to them: the
chain's own ceiling is at most 0.0458 W. -/
theorem measured_ceiling_le :
    measured.aerobic.eta * measured.aerobic.oxycaloric * measured.aerobic.cardiacOutput *
      measured.aerobic.arterialO2 ≤ 0.0458 := aerobicCeiling_le measured.aerobic

/-- The two lethal levers the genotype thread states in hours: *ezh2* (death 48 hpf, fin absence scored at
48 hpf) and *wls* (death by 12 dpf = 288 hpf, ray parameters from 45 dpf = 1080 hpf). Neither phenotype can
be scored in a living animal. -/
theorem ezh2_cannot_be_scored : ¬ CanScore 48 48 := cannot_score_of_lethal_before (by norm_num)

theorems.name: measured_ceiling_le
theorems.doc: The measured aerobic proxies are inside the measured ranges, so the ceiling theorem applies to them: the chain's own ceiling is at most 0.0458 W.
theorems.statement:
theorem measured_ceiling_le :
    measured.aerobic.eta * measured.aerobic.oxycaloric * measured.aerobic.cardiacOutput *
      measured.aerobic.arterialO2 ≤ 0.0458 := aerobicCeiling_le measured.aerobic

/-- The two lethal levers the genotype thread states in hours: *ezh2* (death 48 hpf, fin absence scored at
48 hpf) and *wls* (death by 12 dpf = 288 hpf, ray parameters from 45 dpf = 1080 hpf). Neither phenotype can
be scored in a living animal. -/
theorem ezh2_cannot_be_scored : ¬ CanScore 48 48 := cannot_score_of_lethal_before (by norm_num)

theorem wls_rays_cannot_be_scored : ¬ CanScore 288 1080 := cannot_score_of_lethal_before (by norm_num)

end Empirical

theorems.name: ezh2_cannot_be_scored
theorems.doc: The two lethal levers the genotype thread states in hours: *ezh2* (death 48 hpf, fin absence scored at 48 hpf) and *wls* (death by 12 dpf = 288 hpf, ray parameters from 45 dpf = 1080 hpf). Neither phenotype can be scored in a living animal.
theorems.statement:
theorem ezh2_cannot_be_scored : ¬ CanScore 48 48 := cannot_score_of_lethal_before (by norm_num)

theorem wls_rays_cannot_be_scored : ¬ CanScore 288 1080 := cannot_score_of_lethal_before (by norm_num)

end Empirical
end Delphi

theorems.name: wls_rays_cannot_be_scored
theorems.statement:
theorem wls_rays_cannot_be_scored : ¬ CanScore 288 1080 := cannot_score_of_lethal_before (by norm_num)

end Empirical
end Delphi

theorems.name: fixedBy_tendsto
theorems.statement:
theorem fixedBy_tendsto (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    Tendsto (fun t => C.fixedBy t i) atTop (nhds (C.fixationProbability i))

theorems.name: fixationProbability_ge
theorems.doc: **Lower bound on fixation when selection does not oppose the mutant.** A lineage starting from `i` of `M` copies in a favored chain is eventually fixed with probability at least `i / M`.
theorems.statement:
theorem fixationProbability_ge (hM : 0 < M) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M ≤ C.fixationProbability i

theorems.name: fixationProbability_le_one
theorems.statement: theorem fixationProbability_le_one (i : Fin (M + 1)) : C.fixationProbability i ≤ 1

theorems.name: wrightFisherSelection_fixation_one_ge
theorems.doc: **A new mutant that selection does not oppose fixes with probability at least `1 / M`** under Wright–Fisher sampling, for every `s ≥ 0`.
theorems.statement:
theorem wrightFisherSelection_fixation_one_ge (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    1 / (M : ℝ) ≤ (wrightFisherSelection M hM s hs).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)

theorems.name: wrightFisher_toFavored_fixedBy
theorems.doc: The neutral Wright–Fisher chain, viewed as a favored chain, has the same `fixedBy`.
theorems.statement:
theorem wrightFisher_toFavored_fixedBy (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    (wrightFisher M hM).toFavored.fixedBy t i = (wrightFisher M hM).fixedBy t i := rfl

/-! ### Expected substitutions over `T` generations -/

/-- Expected number of substitutions over `T` generations: Kimura's rate `M μ u` (new mutants per
generation × fixation probability of each, independent fates) summed over `T` generations. A
definition, not a theorem: linkage, interference and changing `M` are excluded by it. -/
def expectedSubstitutions (M : ℕ) (μ u : ℝ) (T : ℕ) : ℝ := substitutionRate M μ u * T

/-- **The neutral budget is `μ T`, whatever the population size.** -/
theorem neutral_expectedSubstitutions (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) (T : ℕ) :

theorems.name: neutral_expectedSubstitutions
theorems.doc: **The neutral budget is `μ T`, whatever the population size.**
theorems.statement:
theorem neutral_expectedSubstitutions (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) (T : ℕ) :
    expectedSubstitutions M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) T = μ * T

theorems.name: favored_expectedSubstitutions_ge
theorems.doc: **Floor:** for any favored chain (neutral, or selection for the mutant) the expected number of substitutions over `T` generations is at least the neutral budget `μ T`.
theorems.statement:
theorem favored_expectedSubstitutions_ge (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (C : FavoredChain M) (μ : ℝ)
    (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (T : ℕ) :
    μ * T ≤ expectedSubstitutions M μ (C.fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) T

theorems.name: expectedSubstitutions_le
theorems.doc: **Ceiling:** with any fixation probability `u ≤ 1`, the expected number of substitutions over `T` generations is at most the mutation supply `M μ T`. This is where the population size enters.
theorems.statement:
theorem expectedSubstitutions_le (M : ℕ) (μ u : ℝ) (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hu : u ≤ 1) (T : ℕ) :
    expectedSubstitutions M μ u T ≤ (M : ℝ) * μ * T

theorems.name: wrightFisherSelection_substitutions_bounds
theorems.doc: The two bounds together, for Wright–Fisher with any `s ≥ 0`: `μ T ≤ E[substitutions] ≤ M μ T`.
theorems.statement:
theorem wrightFisherSelection_substitutions_bounds (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s)
    (μ : ℝ) (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (T : ℕ) :
    μ * T ≤ expectedSubstitutions M μ
        ((wrightFisherSelection M hM s hs).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) T ∧
      expectedSubstitutions M μ
        ((wrightFisherSelection M hM s hs).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) T ≤ (M : ℝ) * μ * T

theorems.name: select_isFreq
theorems.doc: Selection returns a frequency vector when fitnesses are nonnegative and mean fitness is positive.
theorems.statement:
theorem select_isFreq {p w : ι → ℝ} (hp : IsFreq p) (hw : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i)
    (hmean : 0 < meanFitness p w) : IsFreq (select p w)

theorems.name: fisher_fundamental_theorem
theorems.doc: **Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection** (haploid locus, partial change). The change in mean fitness over one generation of selection, with fitnesses held fixed, equals the variance in fitness divided by the mean fitness.
theorems.statement:
theorem fisher_fundamental_theorem {p w : ι → ℝ} (hp : IsFreq p)
    (hmean : 0 < meanFitness p w) :
    meanFitness (select p w) w - meanFitness p w = variance p w / meanFitness p w

theorems.name: fisher_fundamental_theorem'
theorems.doc: The same statement in the form Fisher wrote it: `Δ w̄ · w̄ = V`.
theorems.statement:
theorem fisher_fundamental_theorem' {p w : ι → ℝ} (hp : IsFreq p)
    (hmean : 0 < meanFitness p w) :
    (meanFitness (select p w) w - meanFitness p w) * meanFitness p w = variance p w

theorems.name: mean_fitness_nondecreasing
theorems.doc: Corollary: under fixed fitnesses, mean fitness never decreases.
theorems.statement:
theorem mean_fitness_nondecreasing {p w : ι → ℝ} (hp : IsFreq p)
    (hmean : 0 < meanFitness p w) :
    meanFitness p w ≤ meanFitness (select p w) w

theorems.name: powerLaw_ratio
theorems.statement:
theorem powerLaw_ratio {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (h : PowerLaw f a b) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    f L₂ / f L₁ = (L₂ / L₁) ^ b

theorems.name: powerLaw_log
theorems.statement:
theorem powerLaw_log {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (h : PowerLaw f a b) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (f L₂ / f L₁) = b * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

theorems.name: powerLaw_div
theorems.doc: A quotient of power laws is a power law with the difference of the exponents.
theorems.statement:
theorem powerLaw_div {f g : ℝ → ℝ} {a₁ b₁ a₂ b₂ : ℝ} (hf : PowerLaw f a₁ b₁) (hg : PowerLaw g a₂ b₂) :
    PowerLaw (fun L => f L / g L) (a₁ / a₂) (b₁ - b₂)

theorems.name: cubeLaw_powerLaw
theorems.doc: The cube law is the power law with exponent `3`.
theorems.statement: theorem cubeLaw_powerLaw {W : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : CubeLaw W k) : PowerLaw W k 3

theorems.name: vmin_powerLaw_log
theorems.doc: Under power laws for weight and lifting area with constant `ρ`, `C_L,max`, the minimum-speed exponent is `(b_W - b_S)/2`. With Davenport's exponents this is `(2.981 - 1.834)/2`, not the isometric `1/2`.
theorems.statement:
theorem vmin_powerLaw_log {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {aW bW aS bS ρ Cmax : ℝ} (hW : PowerLaw W aW bW) (hS : PowerLaw S aS bS)
    (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂) / vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁)) = (bW - bS) / 2 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

theorems.name: climbRate_le
theorems.doc: **Climb bound.** If the available mechanical power is spent on level flight, on raising the weight at vertical speed `c`, and on non-negative losses, then `c ≤ (P_avail - P_req)/W`.
theorems.statement:
theorem climbRate_le {W Pavail Preq c loss : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hbal : Pavail = Preq + W * c + loss)
    (hloss : 0 ≤ loss) : c ≤ climbRate W Pavail Preq

theorems.name: climb_nonneg_iff
theorems.statement: theorem climb_nonneg_iff {W Pavail Preq : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) : 0 ≤ climbRate W Pavail Preq ↔ Preq ≤ Pavail

theorems.name: glide_range_le
theorems.doc: **Steady-glide range.** With no thrust, lift equal to weight, `L/D ≤ (L/D)_max` and the potential energy `W h` spent on drag work `D x` plus non-negative losses, the horizontal distance is at most `h (L/D)_max`.
theorems.statement:
theorem glide_range_le {W h D x LDmax loss Lift : ℝ} (_hW : 0 < W) (hD : 0 < D) (hh : 0 ≤ h)
    (hlift : Lift = W) (hLD : Lift / D ≤ LDmax) (henergy : W * h = D * x + loss) (hloss : 0 ≤ loss) :
    x ≤ h * LDmax

theorems.name: glide_range_le_groundEffect
theorems.doc: **Ground effect.** If flying near the surface reduces drag by a fraction `δ` (`D_ge = (1 - δ) D`, `0 ≤ δ < 1`) and leaves lift unaffected, the range bound becomes `h (L/D)_max / (1 - δ)`. Park and Choi (2010) measured `δ` of 0.09 to 0.14 for a flying-fish model; the number enters only as a candidate input.
theorems.statement:
theorem glide_range_le_groundEffect {W h D x LDmax loss Lift δ : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hD : 0 < D) (hh : 0 ≤ h)
    (_hδ0 : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ1 : δ < 1) (hlift : Lift = W) (hLD : Lift / D ≤ LDmax)
    (henergy : W * h = (1 - δ) * D * x + loss) (hloss : 0 ≤ loss) : x ≤ h * LDmax / (1 - δ)

theorems.name: aerobic_le_Ca
theorems.statement:
theorem aerobic_le_Ca {η E Q Ca Cv : ℝ} (hη : 0 ≤ η) (hE : 0 ≤ E) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hCv : 0 ≤ Cv) :
    aerobicPower η E Q Ca Cv ≤ η * E * Q * Ca

theorems.name: aerobic_le_metabolic
theorems.statement:
theorem aerobic_le_metabolic {η E Q Ca Cv : ℝ} (hη : 0 ≤ η) (hη1 : η ≤ 1) (hE : 0 ≤ E) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hCv : 0 ≤ Cv)
    (hCa : 0 ≤ Ca) : aerobicPower η E Q Ca Cv ≤ E * Q * Ca

theorems.name: sustained_le
theorems.doc: **Sustained power bound.** A sustained mechanical power supplied aerobically is at most `η E Q Ca`.
theorems.statement:
theorem sustained_le {P η E Q Ca Cv : ℝ} (hη : 0 ≤ η) (hE : 0 ≤ E) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hCv : 0 ≤ Cv)
    (hsus : P ≤ aerobicPower η E Q Ca Cv) : P ≤ η * E * Q * Ca

theorems.name: sustained_flight_requires
theorems.doc: **Sustained flight needs enough oxygen.** If flight at speed `v` needs `P_req = W v / (L/D)` and the sustained power is aerobic, then `P_req ≤ η E Q Ca`.
theorems.statement:
theorem sustained_flight_requires {W v LD P η E Q Ca Cv : ℝ} (hη : 0 ≤ η) (hE : 0 ≤ E) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hCv : 0 ≤ Cv)
    (hsus : P ≤ aerobicPower η E Q Ca Cv) (hflight : powerRequired W v LD ≤ P) :
    powerRequired W v LD ≤ η * E * Q * Ca

theorems.name: climb_le_aerobic
theorems.doc: **Climb under an aerobic supply.** `c ≤ (η E Q Ca - P_req) / W`.
theorems.statement:
theorem climb_le_aerobic {W Preq c loss P η E Q Ca Cv : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hη : 0 ≤ η) (hE : 0 ≤ E) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q)
    (hCv : 0 ≤ Cv) (hsus : P ≤ aerobicPower η E Q Ca Cv) (hbal : P = Preq + W * c + loss) (hloss : 0 ≤ loss) :
    c ≤ (η * E * Q * Ca - Preq) / W

theorems.name: powerLaw_crossover
theorems.doc: **Crossover.** If demand `D L = a₁ L^{b₁}` and supply `S L = a₂ L^{b₂}` with `b₂ < b₁`, there is a size above which supply falls short of demand. With `b₁ = 7/2` (R5) this is Thompson's size limit for flight under any physiological supply exponent below `7/2`; the muscle premise (`b₂ = 3`) is one instance.
theorems.statement:
theorem powerLaw_crossover {D S : ℝ → ℝ} {a₁ b₁ a₂ b₂ : ℝ} (hD : PowerLaw D a₁ b₁) (hS : PowerLaw S a₂ b₂)
    (hb : b₂ < b₁) : ∃ Ls : ℝ, 0 < Ls ∧ ∀ L, Ls < L → S L < D L

theorems.name: minSubst_le
theorems.doc: `minSubst` is a lower bound on the distance between any two codons of the two amino acids.
theorems.statement:
theorem minSubst_le {a b : AminoAcid} {c d : Codon} (hc : code c = a) (hd : code d = b) :
    minSubst a b ≤ hamming c d

theorems.name: claimed_substitutions_rules_out
theorems.doc: **A missense claim with too few substitutions is impossible.**
theorems.statement:
theorem claimed_substitutions_rules_out {a b : AminoAcid} {n : ℕ} (h : n < minSubst a b) :
    ¬ ∃ c d : Codon, code c = a ∧ code d = b ∧ hamming c d ≤ n

theorems.name: phe_leu_one
theorems.doc: Phe to Leu needs one substitution (e.g. UUU to UUA): the slc43a2a F326L of Daane et al. 2021 is one SNP away.
theorems.statement:
theorem phe_leu_one : minSubst Phe Leu = 1 := by decide +kernel

/-- Trp to Stop needs one; Met to Trp needs two: examples the table decides. -/
theorem trp_stop_one : minSubst Trp Stop = 1 := by decide +kernel
theorem met_trp_two : minSubst Met Trp = 2 := by decide +kernel

/-! ### Developmental ordering -/

open Blueprint in
/-- A `develops_from` graph is well-ordered when every derivative is staged strictly after its precursor
(`stage` is the level; edge `(derivative, precursor)`). Then it is acyclic. -/
theorem devOrdered_acyclic (g : Graph ℕ) (h : g.LevelsDown) : g.Acyclic := g.acyclic_of_levelsDown h

theorems.name: trp_stop_one
theorems.doc: Trp to Stop needs one; Met to Trp needs two: examples the table decides.
theorems.statement:
theorem trp_stop_one : minSubst Trp Stop = 1 := by decide +kernel
theorem met_trp_two : minSubst Met Trp = 2 := by decide +kernel

/-! ### Developmental ordering -/

open Blueprint in
/-- A `develops_from` graph is well-ordered when every derivative is staged strictly after its precursor
(`stage` is the level; edge `(derivative, precursor)`). Then it is acyclic. -/
theorem devOrdered_acyclic (g : Graph ℕ) (h : g.LevelsDown) : g.Acyclic := g.acyclic_of_levelsDown h
