theorems.name: met_trp_two
theorems.statement:
theorem met_trp_two : minSubst Met Trp = 2 := by decide +kernel

/-! ### Developmental ordering -/

open Blueprint in
/-- A `develops_from` graph is well-ordered when every derivative is staged strictly after its precursor
(`stage` is the level; edge `(derivative, precursor)`). Then it is acyclic. -/
theorem devOrdered_acyclic (g : Graph ℕ) (h : g.LevelsDown) : g.Acyclic := g.acyclic_of_levelsDown h

open Blueprint in
/-- The decidable check: every edge strictly down in stage, i.e. no part staged before its precursor. -/
def devOrderedB (g : Graph ℕ) : Bool := g.levelsDownB

theorems.name: devOrdered_acyclic
theorems.doc: A `develops_from` graph is well-ordered when every derivative is staged strictly after its precursor (`stage` is the level; edge `(derivative, precursor)`). Then it is acyclic.
theorems.statement:
theorem devOrdered_acyclic (g : Graph ℕ) (h : g.LevelsDown) : g.Acyclic := g.acyclic_of_levelsDown h

open Blueprint in
/-- The decidable check: every edge strictly down in stage, i.e. no part staged before its precursor. -/
def devOrderedB (g : Graph ℕ) : Bool := g.levelsDownB

open Blueprint in
theorem devOrdered_of_check (g : Graph ℕ) (h : devOrderedB g = true) :
    (∀ a b, g.Edge a b → g.level b < g.level a) ∧ g.Acyclic

theorems.name: devOrdered_of_check
theorems.statement:
theorem devOrdered_of_check (g : Graph ℕ) (h : devOrderedB g = true) :
    (∀ a b, g.Edge a b → g.level b < g.level a) ∧ g.Acyclic

theorems.name: closure_of_check
theorems.statement:
theorem closure_of_check {mapped changed : List String} (h : closureB mapped changed = true) :
    ∀ n ∈ mapped, n ∈ changed

theorems.name: closure_violated
theorems.doc: A change set that omits a mapped node violates closure.
theorems.statement:
theorem closure_violated {mapped changed : List String} {n : String} (hn : n ∈ mapped) (hc : n ∉ changed) :
    closureB mapped changed = false

theorems.name: expectedWaitingTime_neutral
theorems.statement:
theorem expectedWaitingTime_neutral (N : ℝ) (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) :
    expectedWaitingTime N M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) = N / μ

theorems.name: expectedWaitingTime_bounds
theorems.doc: With `1/M ≤ u ≤ 1`, the waiting time lies between `N/(M μ)` and `N/μ`.

theorems.name: too_little_time_rules_out
theorems.doc: **Too little time.** An available time `T` below `N/(M μ)` cannot suffice even if every mutant fixed.

theorems.name: haldane_time_lower
theorems.doc: Under Haldane's hypothesis, `N` selected substitutions need at least `c N / e` generations.
theorems.statement: theorem haldane_time_lower {N T e c : ℝ} (h : HaldaneCost N T e c) (he : 0 < e) : c * N / e ≤ T

theorems.name: haldane_rules_out
theorems.statement: theorem haldane_rules_out {N T e c : ℝ} (h : HaldaneCost N T e c) (he : 0 < e) (hT : T < c * N / e) : False

theorems.name: fixedBy_sub_le
theorems.doc: **Neutral fixation probability (quantitative form).** For some `ρ < 1`, the probability of fixation by generation `t` is within `ρ ^ t` of `i / M`.
theorems.statement:
theorem fixedBy_sub_le (hM : 0 < M) :
    ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 ≤ ρ ∧ ρ < 1 ∧
      ∀ t (i : Fin (M + 1)), |C.fixedBy t i - ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M| ≤ ρ ^ t

theorems.name: fixedBy_tendsto
theorems.doc: **Neutral fixation probability (Kimura 1962, neutral case).** A neutral lineage that starts with `i` of `M` copies is eventually fixed with probability `i / M`.
theorems.statement:
theorem fixedBy_tendsto (hM : 0 < M) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    Tendsto (fun t => C.fixedBy t i) atTop (𝓝 (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M))

theorems.name: fixationProbability_eq
theorems.statement:
theorem fixationProbability_eq (hM : 0 < M) (i : Fin (M + 1)) :
    C.fixationProbability i = ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) / M

theorems.name: wrightFisher_fixation_one
theorems.doc: **Wright–Fisher fixation probability of a new neutral mutant is `1 / M`.**
theorems.statement:
theorem wrightFisher_fixation_one (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) :
    (wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM) = 1 / M

theorems.name: neutral_substitution_rate
theorems.doc: **Kimura (1968).** Under neutral Wright–Fisher evolution, the substitution rate equals the mutation rate, for every population size `M`.
theorems.statement:
theorem neutral_substitution_rate (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) :
    substitutionRate M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixationProbability (oneCopy M hM)) = μ

theorems.name: neutral_substitution_rate_diploid
theorems.doc: The same statement for a diploid population of `N` individuals (`M = 2N` gene copies): `k = 2Nμ · 1/(2N) = μ`, exactly the formula in the claim's notation.
theorems.statement:
theorem neutral_substitution_rate_diploid (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (μ : ℝ) :
    substitutionRate (2 * N) μ
      ((wrightFisher (2 * N) (by omega)).fixationProbability (oneCopy (2 * N) (by omega))) = μ

theorems.name: neutral_substitution_rate_tendsto
theorems.doc: Limit form, with no `limUnder`: the expected number of substitutions per generation attributable to mutants that are fixed by generation `t` converges to `μ`.
theorems.statement:
theorem neutral_substitution_rate_tendsto (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (μ : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun t => substitutionRate M μ ((wrightFisher M hM).fixedBy t (oneCopy M hM)))
      atTop (𝓝 μ)

theorems.name: twofold_cost_of_sex
theorems.doc: **Twofold cost of sex.** With equal fecundity and a `1 : 1` sex ratio, the odds of asexual to sexual females double every generation. Fecundity cancels.
theorems.statement:
theorem twofold_cost_of_sex {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) :
    odds (asexualNext q f) = 2 * odds q

theorems.name: asexualNext_mem
theorems.doc: The next-generation fraction stays strictly between `0` and `1`, so the identity can be iterated.
theorems.statement:
theorem asexualNext_mem {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) :
    0 < asexualNext q f ∧ asexualNext q f < 1

theorems.name: asexualAfter_mem
theorems.statement:
theorem asexualAfter_mem {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) (n : ℕ) :
    0 < asexualAfter q f n ∧ asexualAfter q f n < 1

theorems.name: twofold_cost_of_sex_n
theorems.doc: After `n` generations the odds of asexual to sexual females are `2 ^ n` times the initial odds: an asexual lineage doubles its relative share every generation unless sex brings a compensating twofold advantage.
theorems.statement:
theorem twofold_cost_of_sex_n {q f : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hf : 0 < f) (n : ℕ) :
    odds (asexualAfter q f n) = 2 ^ n * odds q

theorems.name: q10_ratio
theorems.statement:
theorem q10_ratio {X0 Q10 Tref T₁ T₂ : ℝ} (hX : X0 ≠ 0) (hQ : 0 < Q10) :
    q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T₂ / q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T₁ = Q10 ^ ((T₂ - T₁) / 10)

theorems.name: q10_log
theorems.statement:
theorem q10_log {X0 Q10 Tref T₁ T₂ : ℝ} (hX : X0 ≠ 0) (hQ : 0 < Q10) :
    Real.log (q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T₂ / q10Scale X0 Q10 Tref T₁) = (T₂ - T₁) / 10 * Real.log Q10

theorems.name: sphereWallStress_mono
theorems.doc: At fixed pressure and thickness, wall stress grows with radius.
theorems.statement:
theorem sphereWallStress_mono {P t r₁ r₂ : ℝ} (hP : 0 < P) (ht : 0 < t) (h : r₁ ≤ r₂) :
    sphereWallStress P r₁ t ≤ sphereWallStress P r₂ t

theorems.name: laplace_pressure_limit
theorems.doc: **Laplace pressure limit.** A thin spherical wall of strength `σmax` and thickness `t` holds at most `2 σmax t / r`: the pressure limit falls as `1/r`.
theorems.statement:
theorem laplace_pressure_limit {P r t σmax : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (ht : 0 < t) (hσ : sphereWallStress P r t ≤ σmax) :
    P ≤ 2 * σmax * t / r

theorems.name: hoop_pressure_limit
theorems.statement:
theorem hoop_pressure_limit {P r t σmax : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (ht : 0 < t) (hσ : hoopStress P r t ≤ σmax) :
    P ≤ σmax * t / r

theorems.name: areaLaw_ratio
theorems.doc: **R2, area law.**
theorems.statement:
theorem areaLaw_ratio {S : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : AreaLaw S k) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    S L₂ / S L₁ = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 2

theorems.name: wingLoading_ratio
theorems.doc: **R3, wing loading.** Weight per unit area grows linearly with size.
theorems.statement:
theorem wingLoading_ratio {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ}
    (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : (W L₂ / S L₂) / (W L₁ / S L₁) = L₂ / L₁

theorems.name: areaLaw_log
theorems.doc: The `log` form of R2: exponent `2`.
theorems.statement:
theorem areaLaw_log {S : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : AreaLaw S k) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (S L₂ / S L₁) = 2 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

theorems.name: wingLoading_log
theorems.doc: The `log` form of R3 (and of stress, below): exponent `1`.
theorems.statement:
theorem wingLoading_log {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ}
    (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : Real.log ((W L₂ / S L₂) / (W L₁ / S L₁)) = 1 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

theorems.name: breakLoad_ratio
theorems.doc: **R7, conclusion 1.** Breaking load scales as `L²`.
theorems.statement:
theorem breakLoad_ratio {A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₃ σ : ℝ} (hA : AreaLaw A k₃) (hσ : 0 < σ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁)
    (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : breakLoad σ A L₂ / breakLoad σ A L₁ = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 2

theorems.name: safetyFactor_eq
theorems.doc: **R7, conclusion 2.** The static safety factor `F_break / W` equals `σ k₃ / (k₁ L)`: it falls as `1/L`.
theorems.statement:
theorem safetyFactor_eq {W A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₃ σ : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hA : AreaLaw A k₃) {L : ℝ}
    (hL : 0 < L) : breakLoad σ A L / W L = σ * k₃ / (k₁ * L)

theorems.name: stress_ratio
theorems.doc: **Stress grows linearly with size**: `(W/A)(L₂)/(W/A)(L₁) = L₂/L₁` (R1 with R2 on the section).
theorems.statement:
theorem stress_ratio {W A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₃ : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hA : AreaLaw A k₃) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ}
    (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : (W L₂ / A L₂) / (W L₁ / A L₁) = L₂ / L₁

theorems.name: safetyFactor_scaled
theorems.doc: The safety factor of the body scaled by `ℓ` is the reference safety factor divided by `ℓ`.
theorems.statement:
theorem safetyFactor_scaled {W A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₃ σ : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hA : AreaLaw A k₃)
    {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    breakLoad σ A L₂ / W L₂ = (breakLoad σ A L₁ / W L₁) / (L₂ / L₁)

theorems.name: cannot_carry
theorems.doc: **Size limit.** Above `L_max = σ k₃ / (k₁ n)` the member cannot carry `n` body weights.
theorems.statement:
theorem cannot_carry {W A : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₃ σ n : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hA : AreaLaw A k₃) (hσ : 0 < σ)
    (hn : 0 < n) {L : ℝ} (hL : σ * k₃ / (k₁ * n) < L) : breakLoad σ A L < n * W L

theorems.name: vmin_le
theorems.doc: **R4, conclusion 1 (exact, no isometry).** Steady lift-supported flight at lift coefficient at most `C_L,max` needs `v ≥ v_min`.
theorems.statement:
theorem vmin_le {ρ S C Cmax W v : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hS : 0 < S) (hC : 0 < C) (hCmax : C ≤ Cmax) (hv : 0 ≤ v)
    (hlift : lift ρ v S C = W) : vmin ρ Cmax W S ≤ v

theorems.name: vmin_ratio
theorems.doc: **R4, conclusion 2.** Under R1, R2 and the same `ρ`, `C_L,max` for every member, `v_min` scales as `√L`.
theorems.statement:
theorem vmin_ratio {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) (hρ : 0 < ρ)
    (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂) / vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁) = Real.sqrt (L₂ / L₁)

theorems.name: vmin_log
theorems.doc: The `log` form of R4: exponent `1/2`.
theorems.statement:
theorem vmin_log {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) (hρ : 0 < ρ)
    (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂) / vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁)) = 1 / 2 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

theorems.name: powerRequired_ratio
theorems.doc: **R5.** At `v_min`, with constant `L/D`, power required scales as `L³ √L`, i.e. `L^3.5`.
theorems.statement:
theorem powerRequired_ratio {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax LD : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂)
    (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) (hLD : 0 < LD) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    powerRequired (W L₂) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂)) LD / powerRequired (W L₁) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁)) LD
      = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 3 * Real.sqrt (L₂ / L₁)

theorems.name: powerRequired_log
theorems.doc: The `log` form of R5: exponent `7/2`.
theorems.statement:
theorem powerRequired_log {W S : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ ρ Cmax LD : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂)
    (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) (hLD : 0 < LD) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (powerRequired (W L₂) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₂) (S L₂)) LD /
      powerRequired (W L₁) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L₁) (S L₁)) LD) = 7 / 2 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

theorems.name: powerAvailable_ratio
theorems.doc: **R6 (as a named hypothesis).** Under Thompson's muscle premise and R1, power available scales as `L³`.
theorems.statement:
theorem powerAvailable_ratio {P M : ℝ → ℝ} {f p k : ℝ} (hP : MusclePowerLaw P M f p) (hM : CubeLaw M k)
    {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) : P L₂ / P L₁ = (L₂ / L₁) ^ 3

theorems.name: powerRatio_eq
theorems.doc: The ratio `P_req / P_avail` equals `c √L` for an explicit positive constant `c`.
theorems.statement:
theorem powerRatio_eq {W S M P : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ kM ρ Cmax LD f p : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁) (hS : AreaLaw S k₂)
    (hM : CubeLaw M kM) (hP : MusclePowerLaw P M f p) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax) (hLD : 0 < LD)
    {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) :
    powerRequired (W L) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L) (S L)) LD / P L
      = k₁ / (LD * f * p * kM) * Real.sqrt (2 * k₁ / (ρ * k₂ * Cmax)) * Real.sqrt L

theorems.name: exists_size_limit
theorems.doc: **Corollary of R5 and R6 (Thompson's "a bird as large as a man could not fly").** There is a size above which the power required exceeds the power available. The size exists; its value is not supplied.
theorems.statement:
theorem exists_size_limit {W S M P : ℝ → ℝ} {k₁ k₂ kM ρ Cmax LD f p : ℝ} (hW : CubeLaw W k₁)
    (hS : AreaLaw S k₂) (hM : CubeLaw M kM) (hP : MusclePowerLaw P M f p) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hCmax : 0 < Cmax)
    (hLD : 0 < LD) : ∃ Ls : ℝ, 0 < Ls ∧ ∀ L, Ls < L → P L < powerRequired (W L) (vmin ρ Cmax (W L) (S L)) LD

theorems.name: bendingStress_ratio_body
theorems.doc: **R9a, conclusion 1 (body-like load).** With the load scaling as the body (`CubeLaw F`), lever arm `∝ L` and similar sections (`Z ∝ L³`), bending stress scales as `L`.
theorems.statement:
theorem bendingStress_ratio_body {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁ = L₂ / L₁

theorems.name: bendingStress_log_body
theorems.doc: The `log` form of R9a: exponent `1`.
theorems.statement:
theorem bendingStress_log_body {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    Real.log (bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁) = 1 * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)

theorems.name: bendingSafety_eq
theorems.doc: **R9a, conclusion 2.** The bending safety factor `σ_max / σ_b` equals `σ_max k_Z / (k_F k_ℓ L)`: it falls as `1/L`.
theorems.statement:
theorem bendingSafety_eq {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ σmax : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) :
    σmax / bendingStress F ℓ Z L = σmax * kZ / (kF * kℓ * L)

theorems.name: bending_cannot_carry
theorems.doc: **Size limit in bending.** Above `L_max,b = σ_max k_Z / (k_F k_ℓ n)` the member cannot carry `n` times its load in bending: the stress at `n` times the load exceeds `σ_max`. Same shape as `cannot_carry`.

theorems.name: bendingStress_ratio_sheet
theorems.doc: **R9b (sheet-like load).** If the load scales as an area (`AreaLaw F`, a lamina of constant thickness), bending stress is independent of size: no size limit follows.
theorems.statement:
theorem bendingStress_ratio_sheet {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : AreaLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁ = 1

theorems.name: bendingStress_log_sheet
theorems.doc: The `log` form of R9b: exponent `0`.
theorems.statement:
theorem bendingStress_log_sheet {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : AreaLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :

theorems.name: froude_ratio
theorems.doc: **R8.** At equal Froude number, speed scales as `√L`.

formalized.label: Neutral substitution rate equals the mutation rate
formalized.statement: For neutral mutations the long-run rate of molecular substitution equals the mutation rate per generation, independent of population size, which yields a molecular clock.
formalized.notation: k = 2N\mu \cdot \frac{1}{2N} = \mu
formalized.context: Assumptions: strictly neutral mutations, mutation rate constant per generation, steady state. Formal status: an exact consequence of the neutral fixation probability. Variation in generation time and weak selection on nearly neutral sites cause departures from strict clock-like rates.

paper.title: Evolutionary Rate at the Molecular Level

kernelChecked: A neutral absorbing chain on {0..M} copies (stochastic, mean-preserving, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state) fixes a mutant with probability i/M, with an explicit geometric error bound at every finite time t.
The Wright-Fisher binomial kernel is such a chain (row sums, mean preservation and absorption proved from Bernstein polynomial identities).
With u = 1/M the defined substitution rate M * mu * u equals mu, also in the diploid 2N form and as the t -> infinity limit.
assumed: Strict neutrality of the mutations.
Constant population size and Wright-Fisher reproduction (non-overlapping generations, multinomial sampling).

Independent fates of mutants: the substitution rate is DEFINED, as in Kimura 1968, as (new mutants per generation) x (fixation probability of one mutant). Interference between lineages is excluded by that definition, not proved absent.
The mutation rate mu per copy per generation is a free parameter; nothing here measures it.

assessments.rationale: The theorem equates k = M·μ·u to μ with u the fixation probability from one copy, matching Kimura’s k = (number of new mutants per generation) × (fixation probability) and μ as mutation rate per copy. It explicitly assumes neutral Wright–Fisher evolution and uses the fixation probability of a single new mutant (u = 1/M), so independence of population size is captured by “for every M.” However, this is narrower than the law’s general neutral setting (it requires Wright–Fisher sampling and a specific neutral Markov chain) and the independence-of-mutations/steady-state assumptions are only implicit in the substitutionRate definition. The result itself (fixation probability equals initial frequency) is nontrivial, not a tautology of the definitions.

formalized.label: Kimura fixation probability of a mutant allele
formalized.statement: The probability that a mutant allele eventually fixes in a finite population depends on its initial frequency, its selective advantage and the effective population size, and equals its initial frequency when it is neutral.
formalized.notation: u(p) = \frac{1-e^{-4N_e s p}}{1-e^{-4N_e s}}; neutral limit u(p) = p, so a new mutant fixes with probability 1/(2N)
formalized.context: Assumptions: diffusion approximation to the Wright-Fisher model, genic (additive) selection with coefficient s, constant effective size N_e, no linkage to other selected sites. Formal status: proved within the diffusion limit.

paper.title: On the probability of fixation of mutant genes in a population

kernelChecked: Fixation probability i/M for any neutral absorbing chain, hence for the exact finite Wright-Fisher chain (Delphi.NeutralChain.fixedBy_tendsto).
assumed: Neutral case only (s = 0). Kimura 1962 with selection in the diffusion limit is not formalised.

assessments.rationale: The Lean theorem asserts that in a neutral setting the eventual fixation probability equals the initial frequency: Tendsto (fun t => C.fixedBy t i) … to ((i : ℝ)/M). This matches the neutral part of Kimura’s claim (u(p) = p), with C.fixedBy modeling fixation probability and i/M the initial frequency. The assumptions are expressed as a general neutral absorbing Markov chain (NeutralChain.neutral, absorb_zero, absorb_last, rowSum), not specifically the Wright–Fisher diffusion with N_e and s; thus they differ from the source context and omit s, N_e. The scope is clearly stated as the neutral case, and the result is substantive rather than definitional.

formalized.note: One haploid or clonal locus with finitely many types, fitnesses held fixed (partial change). In that population the variance in fitness is the additive genetic variance. The diploid average-effect version is not formalised.
formalized.label: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)
formalized.statement: The rate of increase in mean fitness of a population due to natural selection equals its additive genetic variance in fitness at that time.
formalized.notation: \Delta_{NS}\bar{w} = V_A(w)/\bar{w} (discrete generations); \left.\frac{d\bar{m}}{dt}\right|_{NS} = V_A(m) for Malthusian fitness m
formalized.context: Assumptions: the 'partial change' holds average effects of alleles and the environment fixed (Price 1972, Ewens 1989); V_A is the additive genetic variance in fitness. Formal status: proved in this partial-change reading. Read as a claim about the total change in mean fitness it is false under dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or a changing environment.

paper.title: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection

kernelChecked: For one locus with finitely many types, frequencies p (nonneg, summing to 1), fixed fitnesses w and mean fitness > 0: selection p_next = p w / wbar yields wbar_next - wbar = Var(w)/wbar exactly.

formalized.label: Fixation is at least i/M when selection does not oppose the mutant
formalized.statement: In an absorbing chain on 0..M gene copies whose expected copy number never decreases (neutral, or selection for the mutant), a lineage present in i copies is eventually fixed with probability at least i/M. formalized.note: A lower bound only. Neutral chains are favored chains, and for them the bound is attained, so no upper bound in terms of s follows from this module.

Wright-Fisher sampling with success probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), s >= 0, is such a chain (Delphi.wrightFisherSelection), so a single new mutant fixes with probability at least 1/M.
The defined expected count M mu u T equals mu T for the neutral Wright-Fisher chain, is at least mu T for any favored chain, and is at most M mu T for any u <= 1.

Selection enters only through the sampling probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), constant in time and across sites.
mu, T, M are free parameters; the module measures nothing. Which mutations are favored, how many a trait needs, and in what order, are outside it.

formalized.label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground

Hence sustained flight possible at a height is possible at every lower height; above an infeasible height every height is infeasible, so the flyable set is an interval from the ground up to a ceiling; and a design that cannot fly at the ground cannot fly at any height. A larger lifting area lowers the power required at a fixed height.

So nothing here supports reading "the feasible region shrinks with altitude" as the reason a fish cannot fly high: the reason is the oxygen budget at sea level. undefined.selectionCoefficient: Undefined for the transition. The favored-chain theorem needs only that selection does not oppose the mutant (s >= 0); it gives no upper bound that depends on s.
undefined.fractionOfMutationsFavored: Undefined. The floor for adaptive substitutions is stated per favored mutation rate mu_f, which is at most the total rate mu and is not measured.
undefined.requiredSubstitutions: Undefined. 'Substitutions required for a wing' is not a defined quantity; no figure is invented, so the comparison the feasibility question needs cannot be made.

floor.statement: Expected adaptive substitutions over T generations are at least mu_f * T per site, where mu_f is the rate of mutations that selection does not oppose. mu_f is undefined, so the floor is a function of mu_f: at mu_f = mu it equals the neutral budget; at mu_f = 0 it is 0.

ceiling.statement: Expected substitutions over T generations are at most 2 N mu T per site (every mutation that arises fixes). Grows linearly in N and is vacuous for a feasibility question.

comparison.reason: The quantity the budget would have to be compared with, the number of substitutions a wing requires, is undefined; no figure is invented. The floor on adaptive substitutions also depends on the undefined fraction of mutations that selection favours. What is established: the neutral budget and the floor do not depend on N (the parameter the literature constrains least), and the ceiling is vacuous.

kernelChecked: Delphi.FavoredChain.fixationProbability_ge: in an absorbing chain on 0..M copies whose expected copy number never decreases (selection neutral or for the mutant), with positive one-step escape from every interior state, a lineage of i copies fixes with probability at least i/M; the limit exists because fixation is absorbing.
Delphi.wrightFisherSelection_fixation_one_ge: Wright-Fisher sampling with mutant relative fitness 1+s, s >= 0, is such a chain, so one new mutant fixes with probability at least 1/M.
Delphi.neutral_expectedSubstitutions: with the proved neutral fixation probability 1/M, the defined expected count M mu u T equals mu T for every M.
Delphi.favored_expectedSubstitutions_ge and Delphi.expectedSubstitutions_le: for any favored chain mu T <= M mu u T, and for any u <= 1, M mu u T <= M mu T.
assumed: The expected count M mu u T is a definition (Kimura 1968: new mutants per generation times fixation probability, summed over generations). Independent fates, no linkage or interference, constant M, constant mu, constant s and non-overlapping generations enter through that definition and are not proved.

The numbers for T, mu, G and N come from the literature sources named in lean/bound/parameters.json, none of which measures Exocoetidae for mu or generation time; the fossil first appearance is a minimum age, and it rests on two PBDB occurrence records from one publication (Bannikov 2014, Monte Bolca); the next-oldest record (David 1946) is 37.71 to 33.9 Ma and is carried as a sensitivity case.
The selection coefficient, the fraction of mutations selection favours, and the number of substitutions a wing requires are undefined; the result is a one-sided budget with nothing to compare it to.
Nothing here is about which substitutions, in which genes, or whether they are reachable in sequence; a count of fixations is not a path to a wing.

thompsonTest.passCriterion: Pre-registered. REFUTES if, for either sex, b lies outside [2.5, 3.5] OR the cubic model's R^2 on the age-bin weight curve is < 0.90. MIXED is not possible under this rule except as follows: if the two sexes disagree (one passes, the other fails) the verdict is MIXED. INCONCLUSIVE (data-unavailable) if the files cannot be downloaded.

exponents.label: pooled individuals 0-19 y, OLS (earlier run, NHANES 2007-2018)

caveats: The free exponent is below 3 in both sexes (2.74 and 2.86) and the male CI excludes 3, so weight grows a little slower than the cube of stature across childhood; Thompson's 'mainly (though not wholly)' is borne out literally: the cube reproduces the weight curve with R^2 of 0.98-0.99 but is not exact.
Cross-sectional population means from 2013-2018 US children, who are heavier at given height than Thompson's early-20th-century tables; the exponent, not the constant k, is what the claim concerns.
Binned means over 18 ages leave 16 degrees of freedom; the CI reflects bin-to-bin scatter, not individual variation.

Post-hoc discriminating-power check (perturbation.py, added 2026-10-31 after the result; simulation, not observation): with the observed mean heights and bin scatter, the pre-registered rule passes in 100% (males) and 99.95% (females) of 2000 simulations under the cube law, in 0% under an exponent of 2 or 4, and in about 47 to 49% at the band edges 2.5 and 3.5; so the rule rejects surface-law and fourth-power alternatives and is indifferent only at its own pre-registered boundaries.

Cross-check (cross_check.py, added 2026-10-31 after the result; verdict unchanged): the collaborator swarm's test of this claim (origin/main, run cursor/claim-tests-thompson-efb7, NHANES 2007-2018, ages 0 to 19.99 with recumbent length under 24 months) reports a pooled individual-level exponent of 2.408 (95% CI 2.399 to 2.416, n = 23540) and 'mixed'. On this test's own sample the individual-level exponent is 2.755 (CI 2.736 to 2.775, n = 9715; males 2.716, females 2.812), within 0.03 of the age-bin values, so the unit of analysis (bins versus individuals) is not the cause. The cause is the age range: the collaborator's own 2-20 year window gives 2.736 (CI 2.723 to 2.750, n = 19714), reproducing this test, while their 0-2 year window gives 2.098 and pulls the pooled exponent below the 2.5 edge of the band both tests pre-registered. The 'supports' verdict is therefore conditional on the scope fixed at pre-registration (ages 2 to 19, standing stature); including infancy in Thompson's 'during growth' makes it 'mixed'. Whether infancy is inside the claim is a reading of the claim, not a measurement.

constraints.framing: A theorem eliminates candidates, not open problems: a candidate is a proposed answer or design that commits to quantities the theorem forbids. Three states: eliminated (the violated relation with the numbers, kernel-checked where marked), consistent (not ruled out by these theorems; never "feasible"), cannot-rule (a required input or assumption is missing). An elimination holds only under the law's own assumptions, listed per constraint; three of the four original statements were judged narrower in scope than their claims by the assessor, and a candidate eliminated by a narrower statement is eliminated only under that statement's assumptions.

assumptions.neutral_wright_fisher: strictly neutral mutations, constant population size, Wright-Fisher reproduction, independent mutant fates (lean/Delphi/Kimura.lean header)
assumptions.wright_fisher_selection: Wright-Fisher sampling with relative fitness 1+s for the mutant, s constant (lean/Delphi/Favored.lean header)
assumptions.independent_fates_definition: the expected count is Kimura's definition rate x generations: independent fates, constant M, mu and s, no linkage (lean/Delphi/Favored.lean header)
assumptions.fixed_fitnesses_one_locus: one haploid or clonal locus, fixed fitnesses within the step, infinite population, no mutation (lean/Delphi/Fisher.lean header)
assumptions.equal_fecundity_1to1: equal fecundity of sexual and asexual females, a 1:1 sex ratio, males contributing nothing, discrete generations (lean/Delphi/MaynardSmith.lean header)
assumptions.isometric_constant_density: the same body family scaled without change of shape or density, so W = k L^3 (lean/Delphi/Thompson.lean header)
assumptions.isometric_areas: the area in question (lifting area, load-bearing cross-section, exchange surface) scales as k L^2 across the family (AreaLaw, lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean)
assumptions.same_material: the breaking stress σ is the same for every member of the family (R7)
assumptions.axial_loading: the member fails under axial load σ A; bending is not formalised
assumptions.lift_supported_flight: steady flight with lift ½ ρ v² S C_L equal to weight and 0 < C_L ≤ C_L,max (R4)
assumptions.constant_lift_coefficient_max_and_densit: C_L,max and ρ the same for every member of the family (R4 scaling)
assumptions.constant_lift_to_drag: L/D the same for every member and flight at v_min (R5)
assumptions.muscle_power_premise: Thompson's premise, contested: muscle mass a constant fraction f of body mass and mass-specific power p constant (R6, MusclePowerLaw)
assumptions.equal_froude_number: the compared animals move at equal Froude number v²/(g L) (R8)
assumptions.linear_elastic_slender_beam: Euler-Bernoulli beam: σ_b = M_b / Z with M_b = F ℓ, static load (R9)
assumptions.similar_sections: geometrically similar cross-sections, Z = k_Z d^3 with d ∝ L (R9)
assumptions.lever_arm_proportional: the lever arm ℓ scales as L (R9)
assumptions.body_like_load: the transverse load scales as the body, F ∝ L^3 (R9a; isometric mass with constant density)
assumptions.sheet_like_load: the transverse load is a lamina of constant thickness, F ∝ L^2 (R9b)
assumptions.power_law_forms: weight and lifting area each follow a single power law in L over the range in question (PowerLaw)
assumptions.power_balance_nonneg_losses: available mechanical power = level-flight power + W × climb rate + non-negative losses
assumptions.steady_unpowered_glide: one steady glide, no thrust, lift equal to weight, L/D ≤ (L/D)max, potential energy spent on drag work plus non-negative losses; ground effect only as a stated drag reduction
assumptions.fitted_mass_exponent_band: empirical entry E2: the mass exponent of a fitted field study lies in [2.90, 3.02] (six fitted rows of five species, the male-only outlier excluded and named); the candidate accepts the observation
assumptions.teleost_measured_ranges: empirical entry E3: efficiency, oxycaloric equivalent, cardiac output and arterial O2 content lie inside the measured teleost ranges the physiology chain cites, so the sustained aerobic ceiling at 0.06 kg is at most 0.0458 W
assumptions.no_aerial_uptake: empirical entry E4: gills do not ventilate in air, so airborne aerobic work is paid out of the O2 store carried into the air
assumptions.lethality_before_scoring: empirical entry E7: an animal that the source reports dead at or before the scoring stage cannot show the scored phenotype
assumptions.fick_aerobic_supply: sustained mechanical power ≤ η × E_O2 × Q × (Ca − Cv) with 0 ≤ Cv ≤ Ca, 0 ≤ η ≤ 1 (Fick; aerobic, not burst)
assumptions.standard_genetic_code: the standard genetic code as tabulated in lean/Delphi/Genotype.lean (no alternative or mitochondrial code, no selenocysteine, no editing); one codon per amino acid position
assumptions.map_links_are_the_gene_reach: the nodes the genotype map links a gene to are the nodes an edit to that gene may change; the map records links, not dynamics, so this bounds what a picture may hide, never how much a node changes
assumptions.zfin_stage_order: the ZFIN stage-series ids order the stages of development (they are assigned in developmental order for the main series), and develops_from means the derivative appears no earlier than its precursor
assumptions.independent_sequential_fixations: the required substitutions fix one after another at Kimura's rate M μ u with constant M, μ and u, 1/M ≤ u ≤ 1 (neutral or favoured, by the Favored module); no linkage, no standing variation, no recombination of partial solutions
assumptions.haldane_cost_of_selection: Haldane 1957's accounting: substitutions by selection over T generations are at most e T / c, with reproductive excess e and cost per substitution c. A contested model, carried as a named hypothesis and never proved here

list.label: Neutral substitution rate equals the mutation rate
list.property: the long-run rate at which neutral mutations become substitutions, relative to the mutation rate
list.rule: eliminated when the committed intervals for k and mu are disjoint; consistent when they overlap
list.canEliminate: only a candidate that commits to a neutral substitution rate different from its mutation rate (for example a neutral clock that scales with population size)

kernelChecked: A neutral absorbing chain on {0..M} copies (stochastic, mean-preserving, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state) fixes a mutant with probability i/M, with an explicit geometric error bound at every finite time t.
The Wright-Fisher binomial kernel is such a chain (row sums, mean preservation and absorption proved from Bernstein polynomial identities).
With u = 1/M the defined substitution rate M * mu * u equals mu, also in the diploid 2N form and as the t -> infinity limit.
assumed: Strict neutrality of the mutations.
Constant population size and Wright-Fisher reproduction (non-overlapping generations, multinomial sampling).

Independent fates of mutants: the substitution rate is DEFINED, as in Kimura 1968, as (new mutants per generation) x (fixation probability of one mutant). Interference between lineages is excluded by that definition, not proved absent.
The mutation rate mu per copy per generation is a free parameter; nothing here measures it.

list.label: Neutral substitution rate equals the mutation rate
list.property: whether neutral substitution rates can differ between lineages that share a mutation rate (for example through population size)
list.rule: applies only when the committed mutation-rate ratio is exactly 1; then eliminated when the committed substitution-rate ratio is not 1
list.canEliminate: a candidate that attributes a difference in neutral substitution rate between lineages to anything other than a difference in mutation rate (population size, for instance)

assumed: Strict neutrality of the mutations.

list.label: Kimura fixation probability of a mutant allele
list.property: the probability that a single new neutral mutant copy is eventually fixed
list.rule: eliminated when 1/M lies outside the committed interval for u
list.canEliminate: only a candidate that commits to a specific contradicting probability; it says nothing about which mutations arise or what they do

kernelChecked: Fixation probability i/M for any neutral absorbing chain, hence for the exact finite Wright-Fisher chain (Delphi.NeutralChain.fixedBy_tendsto).
assumed: Neutral case only (s = 0). Kimura 1962 with selection in the diffusion limit is not formalised.

list.label: Fixation is at least i/M when selection does not oppose the mutant
list.property: the fixation probability of a single new mutant that selection does not oppose
list.rule: eliminated when the committed upper end of u is below 1/M
list.canEliminate: a candidate that says a neutral or favored mutant fixes less often than drift alone allows; it cannot eliminate on the high side (no upper bound in s is proved)

kernelChecked: For any absorbing chain on {0..M} copies with E[X_{t+1} | X_t = i] >= i (stochastic, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state), P(fixed by t) is nondecreasing and bounded, its limit u(i) exists, and u(i) >= i/M (Delphi.FavoredChain.fixationProbability_ge); also u(i) <= 1.
Wright-Fisher sampling with success probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), s >= 0, is such a chain (Delphi.wrightFisherSelection), so a single new mutant fixes with probability at least 1/M.
The defined expected count M mu u T equals mu T for the neutral Wright-Fisher chain, is at least mu T for any favored chain, and is at most M mu T for any u <= 1.
assumed: The expected count is a DEFINITION (rate x generations, independent fates, Kimura 1968); linkage, interference, changing M, changing s and overlapping generations are excluded by it, not shown absent.
Selection enters only through the sampling probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), constant in time and across sites.
mu, T, M are free parameters; the module measures nothing. Which mutations are favored, how many a trait needs, and in what order, are outside it.

list.label: Fixation is at least i/M when selection does not oppose the mutant
list.property: the expected number of substitutions a lineage can accumulate over a given time
list.rule: eliminated when the committed lower end of E exceeds G * M * (upper end of mu) * T
list.canEliminate: a candidate that commits to an expected count above the mutation supply; a realised count, or a count without M, mu and T, cannot be ruled on

list.label: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)
list.property: the change in mean fitness over one round of selection, given the variance in fitness
list.rule: point commitments only: eliminated when delta_wbar * wbar != V exactly; interval commitments fall to C4b
list.canEliminate: a candidate that commits to all three quantities as exact values violating the identity

kernelChecked: For one locus with finitely many types, frequencies p (nonneg, summing to 1), fixed fitnesses w and mean fitness > 0: selection p_next = p w / wbar yields wbar_next - wbar = Var(w)/wbar exactly.
Corollary: mean fitness never decreases under fixed fitnesses.
assumed: Haploid or clonal inheritance, so the variance in fitness IS the additive genetic variance; the diploid average-effect version is not formalised.
Fitnesses constant within the step (partial change): no dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or environmental change.
Infinite population: deterministic frequencies, no drift, no mutation.

list.label: Twofold cost of sex
list.property: how fast an asexual lineage spreads among sexual females
list.rule: point commitments: eliminated when odds(q_n) != 2^n * odds(q_0) exactly on rationals
list.canEliminate: a candidate that commits to a spread faster or slower than the twofold doubling under the stated assumptions

kernelChecked: For 0 < q < 1 and fecundity f > 0 the odds of asexual to sexual females satisfy odds(q_next) = 2 odds(q), and f cancels.
Iterated n generations the odds are 2^n times the initial odds.
assumed: Anisogamy: males contribute nothing to offspring number or survival.
Equal fecundity and viability of sexual and asexual females and of their daughters.
Primary sex ratio exactly 1:1 in sexual broods; discrete non-overlapping generations; infinite population (deterministic fractions).

list.label: Twofold cost of sex

list.rule: eliminated when the committed factor is not exactly 2
list.canEliminate: a candidate that commits to a per-generation odds factor other than 2 under the stated assumptions; a factor of 2 is the theorem and is consistent

list.label: An emitted anatomical blueprint graph is well-formed under its own rules
list.property: the internal coherence of a proposed anatomical design: acyclic part_of, every term reaching the body root, no term excluded by taxon constraints

symbols.D: taxon statements pinned from Ubergraph for it

list.rule: consistent when the generated certificate compiles (kernel-evaluated checker); eliminated when the checker rejects the design, naming the failing condition (plain computation: the completeness direction check = false -> not well-formed is not proved)
list.canEliminate: a design whose part_of graph has a cycle or an orphan, or that keeps a term the pinned taxon statements exclude; it says nothing biological
list.kernelCheckable: on pass (certificate); on rejection the failing condition is reported by plain computation

kernelChecked: Generic (any node type): edges strictly down in level ⟹ the part_of closure is transitive, strictly decreases the level, and is acyclic (Graph.acyclic_of_levelsDown, Graph.transGen_trans, Graph.transGen_level_lt).
Generic: edges closed and every non-root node has a whole ⟹ every node reaches the root (Graph.rooted_of, strong induction on level).
Generic: the Boolean checker is sound for LevelsDown, Closed, Acyclic, Rooted and the taxon conditions (wellFormed_of_check).

Per blueprint: the kernel evaluates the checker on the emitted graph and the pinned taxon rows (decide +kernel), and fixes the distinct-term counts per level and the graph size (lean/Delphi/Certificates/*.lean).
assumed: That Uberon and the Cell Ontology are correct and that Ubergraph served their part_of, subClassOf, never_in_taxon and in_taxon statements correctly and completely on the retrieval date: the graph and the taxon rows are data, pinned by hash and query.
That the five levels (body, organ system, organ, tissue, cell) are the right notion of depth; the theorems use only that edges strictly decrease it.
Nothing about any organism: not that it is real, that the anatomy is correct or complete, that any part was measured, or anything about a transition between forms.

list.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
list.property: how weight scales with a linear dimension under isometric scaling at constant density
list.rule: eliminated when the committed weight-ratio interval is disjoint from the cube of the length-ratio interval
list.canEliminate: the mass side of Galileo's square-cube argument only: a giant with unchanged proportions and density must weigh (L2/L1)^3 times more. Strength scaling as L^2 is NOT formalised, so a candidate claiming the giant can support itself is not ruled out by this theorem

kernelChecked: If W L = k L^3 for all L > 0 with k > 0, then for L1 ≠ L2 the log-log slope (log W L2 − log W L1)/(log L2 − log L1) equals exactly 3 (cubeLaw_loglog_exponent) and W L2 / W L1 = (L2/L1)^3 (cubeLaw_ratio).
Contrapositive: two sizes with a log-log slope b ≠ 3 rule out W = k L^3 for every k (not_cubeLaw_of_exponent_ne_three).
assumed: A single linear dimension L and mass W of one body family; fixed shape and constant density are what W = k L^3 encodes.
Thompson's "mainly (though not wholly)" is not formalised: the theorem is exact, the law is approximate, and the tolerance band [2.5, 3.5] the claim test uses is a decision rule outside the module.
No data enters the module; the measured exponents are read from the claims thread's result files and pointed to.

list.label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
list.property: how an area (lifting surface, cross-section, exchange surface) scales with the linear dimension under isometry
list.rule: eliminated when the committed exponent interval excludes 2
list.canEliminate: a candidate that asserts isometry of the area and an area exponent other than 2; an exponent of 2 is the hypothesis restated and is consistent

kernelChecked: If S L = k L^2 for all L > 0 (AreaLaw) then S(L2)/S(L1) = (L2/L1)^2 and log S(L2)/S(L1) = 2 log(L2/L1) (areaLaw_ratio, areaLaw_log).
With CubeLaw W: (W/S)(L2)/(W/S)(L1) = L2/L1, exponent 1 (wingLoading_ratio, wingLoading_log).
assumed: Isometry of the area and of the mass (constant density): named hypotheses, measured to fail within one flying-fish species (Davenport 1992).
Nothing about which family is isometric; the theorems bound only families that are.

list.property: whether a member of stated cross-section and material can carry a stated load (dimensional, no scaling needed)
list.rule: eliminated when σ A < n W
list.canEliminate: a design that commits to σ, A, W and the load it carries, with σ A < n W

kernelChecked: F_break = σ A: with AreaLaw A and σ > 0, F_break(L2)/F_break(L1) = (L2/L1)^2 (breakLoad_ratio).

With CubeLaw W: F_break/W = σ k3/(k1 L) (safetyFactor_eq); the safety factor of the scaled body is the reference one divided by the length ratio (safetyFactor_scaled); stress W/A scales as L2/L1 (stress_ratio).

assumed: Axial loading (bending has the same L^2 dependence with a different constant; not formalised).
Isometric load-bearing sections and the same material (constant σ): real animals thicken bones with size.
Nothing about any real giant: the checker rules only on a candidate that commits to isometry, the same material and a safety factor.

list.label: Bending strength of an isometric member via the section modulus (R9)
list.property: how bending stress scales with size when the load scales as the body (R9a)

kernelChecked: R9a: with CubeLaw F, LeverLaw ℓ and SectionModulusLaw Z, σ_b(L2)/σ_b(L1) = L2/L1, log exponent 1 (bendingStress_ratio_body, bendingStress_log_body); σ_max/σ_b = σ_max k_Z/(k_F k_ℓ L) (bendingSafety_eq); above σ_max k_Z/(k_F k_ℓ n) the stress at n times the load exceeds σ_max (bending_cannot_carry).

Constant σ_max; static loads only (wind on a leaf is outside the model); which load family applies (R9a or R9b) is empirical and must be committed by the candidate.

list.label: General allometry: measured exponents compose (W = a L^b)
list.property: whether committed weight, area and wing-loading exponents are mutually consistent
list.rule: eliminated when the interval bW − bS is disjoint from the committed bWS interval (separate regressions need intervals; point commitments without error would spuriously eliminate)
list.canEliminate: a candidate committing three exponents that cannot all hold

kernelChecked: PowerLaw f a b ⇒ f(L2)/f(L1) = (L2/L1)^b and log exponent b (powerLaw_ratio, powerLaw_log).
Quotients: PowerLaw (f/g) (a1/a2) (b1 − b2) (powerLaw_div); CubeLaw is PowerLaw with b = 3 (cubeLaw_powerLaw).
Under PowerLaw W and PowerLaw S with constant ρ, C_L,max: the v_min log exponent is (bW − bS)/2 (vmin_powerLaw_log).
assumed: That weight and area follow single power laws over the size range in question with the exponents committed; the fitted exponents are separate regressions with their own errors.
Nothing measured for Exocoetidae enters a statement; the exponents are candidate inputs.

list.label: Sustained mechanical power is bounded by oxygen delivery (Fick) times efficiency
list.property: whether oxygen delivery can sustain level flight at the stated speed
list.relation: η E_O2 Q Ca ≥ W v / (L/D)
list.rule: eliminated when η E Q Ca < W v/(L/D); units must be consistent (E × Q × Ca in watts)
list.canEliminate: a design claiming sustained powered flight its oxygen delivery cannot pay for

kernelChecked: η E Q (Ca − Cv) ≤ η E Q Ca for Cv ≥ 0 (aerobic_le_Ca); ≤ E Q Ca for η ≤ 1 (aerobic_le_metabolic); P ≤ aerobicPower ⇒ P ≤ η E Q Ca (sustained_le).
P_req ≤ P ≤ aerobicPower ⇒ P_req ≤ η E Q Ca (sustained_flight_requires); climb under aerobic supply c ≤ (η E Q Ca − P_req)/W (climb_le_aerobic).
PowerLaw demand and supply with b_supply < b_demand ⇒ ∃ L* > 0, ∀ L > L*, supply < demand (powerLaw_crossover).
assumed: Fick: O2 delivered = Q (Ca − Cv); the oxycaloric equivalent E converts O2 to metabolic power; mechanical power is at most η times it; sustained power is aerobic (anaerobic bursts, oxygen debt, and the glide phase, which needs no muscle power, are outside).
0 ≤ Cv ≤ Ca, 0 ≤ η ≤ 1, Q, E ≥ 0; the supply exponent is whatever the physiology gives, not derived here.

list.label: Climb from excess power and the range of a steady glide
list.property: how far one steady unpowered glide can go from a given height
list.rule: eliminated when x > h (L/D)max/(1 − δ)
list.canEliminate: a claim that a single unpowered glide from height h covers more than the energy bound allows; taxiing thrust, repeated touch-and-go and wind are outside the model and must be committed separately

kernelChecked: Power balance P_avail = P_req + W c + loss with loss ≥ 0 ⇒ c ≤ (P_avail − P_req)/W (climbRate_le); 0 ≤ (P_avail − P_req)/W ⇔ P_req ≤ P_avail (climb_nonneg_iff).
Energy balance W h = D x + loss, loss ≥ 0, lift = W, L/D ≤ (L/D)max ⇒ x ≤ h (L/D)max (glide_range_le); with drag (1 − δ) D ⇒ x ≤ h (L/D)max/(1 − δ) (glide_range_le_groundEffect).
assumed: A single steady glide with no thrust and lift equal to weight; taxiing, repeated touch-and-go, wind and updrafts are outside the model.
Losses non-negative; the ground-effect fraction δ and (L/D)max are inputs.

list.label: Climb from excess power and the range of a steady glide
list.property: the climb rate available from excess power
list.rule: eliminated when c > (P_avail − P_req)/W
list.canEliminate: a powered design claiming a climb rate its excess power cannot deliver

kernelChecked: Power balance P_avail = P_req + W c + loss with loss ≥ 0 ⇒ c ≤ (P_avail − P_req)/W (climbRate_le); 0 ≤ (P_avail − P_req)/W ⇔ P_req ≤ P_avail (climb_nonneg_iff).
Energy balance W h = D x + loss, loss ≥ 0, lift = W, L/D ≤ (L/D)max ⇒ x ≤ h (L/D)max (glide_range_le); with drag (1 − δ) D ⇒ x ≤ h (L/D)max/(1 − δ) (glide_range_le_groundEffect).

list.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance
list.property: whether an amino-acid change is reachable in the claimed number of nucleotide substitutions
list.relation: n ≥ minSubst(a, b), the least Hamming distance between a codon for a and a codon for b
list.rule: eliminated when the claimed count is below minSubst(a, b) over the 64-codon table; consistent when some codon pair is within the claim. The checker decides reachability in the code, not whether the substitution happened
list.canEliminate: a claim that one point mutation produced an amino-acid change the code needs two or three for (for example methionine to tryptophan)

kernelChecked: The standard code as a 64-case table, hamming distance on codons, and minSubst as the least distance over the codons of the two amino acids.
That no codon pair realises a to b in fewer than minSubst a b substitutions, so a claim below that count is impossible.
Each instance by kernel evaluation of the table: Phe to Leu 1, Trp to Stop 1, Met to Trp 2.
assumed: The standard genetic code. Mitochondrial and variant codes differ; selenocysteine insertion and RNA editing are outside the table.
One codon per position, substitutions within that codon; frameshifts, indels and multi-codon changes are not modelled.
That reachability in the code is only reachability: nothing here says a substitution occurred, was favoured, or had the claimed effect.

list.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
list.property: whether an edit to a gene is shown changing every node the map links that gene to
list.relation: every node the map links to the gene is in the set the edit changes
list.rule: eliminated when the map links the gene to a node the edit does not change (the picture would hide a pleiotropic effect); consistent when the changed set covers every linked node. Link sets come from lean/genotype/gene-nodes.json (direct, non-derived links of genotype/fin-subtree.full.json), so an absent node is unstudied, not gene-free
list.canEliminate: a Design Studio view showing a gene edit as a change to one structure when the map links that gene to several

kernelChecked: That the Boolean list-inclusion check is sound (its truth implies every mapped node is changed) and that a single missing node makes it false.
assumed: That the nodes the genotype map links a gene to are the nodes an edit may change: a bound on what a picture may omit, not a model of development.
That an unstudied node is absent from the map: the closure is only as complete as the sources behind it (ZFIN, Bgee), and the fin subtree is zebrafish anatomy.
Nothing about magnitude: the check cannot say how much any node changes, or in which direction.

list.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
list.property: whether a structure is claimed to appear before the precursor it develops from
list.rule: eliminated when the derivative is staged at or before its precursor; consistent when it is staged later. The fin subtree's own develops_from edges are certified separately by lean/genotype/certify-dev.mjs, which the kernel evaluates on the recorded stages
list.canEliminate: a developmental sequence that puts a fin before its fin bud

kernelChecked: That a develops_from graph whose Boolean stage check passes has every derivative staged strictly after its precursor, and is acyclic.
The fin subtree's 8 edges with both stages recorded, by kernel evaluation of the checker on those stages.
assumed: That the ZFIN stage-series ids order development (they are assigned in order for the main series).
That develops_from means the derivative appears no earlier than its precursor.
The 4 edges with an unknown stage are not certified, and nothing here concerns the flying fish.

list.label: The time N independent substitutions need lies between N/(M mu) and N/mu
list.property: whether the stated number of generations can carry the required substitutions at the stated mutation rate
list.rule: eliminated when T < N/(M μ), the fastest the model allows (fixation probability u = 1, every mutant fixed); consistent otherwise. Consistency here is very weak: the neutral case needs N/μ, M times longer, and the model says nothing about whether the substitutions exist or help
list.canEliminate: a claim needing more sequential substitutions than the mutation supply can deliver in the stated time; it cannot eliminate anything for a trait whose required count is undefined, which is the state of every wing claim in this project

kernelChecked: That the expected time for N substitutions at rate M mu u is N/(M mu u), and that for 1/M <= u <= 1 it lies between N/(M mu) and N/mu, with equality at N/mu for the neutral u = 1/M.
That an available time below N/(M mu) contradicts the model even with every mutant fixing.
assumed: Independent sequential fixations at Kimura's definition rate with constant M, mu and u: no linkage, no standing variation, no recombination of partial solutions.
That the number of required substitutions is given. It is not defined for any wing claim here, which is why this bound eliminates nothing about the flying fish.
Nothing about whether the required substitutions exist, are favoured, or produce the trait.

list.label: From Haldane's cost accounting (a hypothesis, not proved here): N substitutions need at least c N / e generations
list.property: whether the population can pay the cost of the required substitutions in the stated time
list.rule: eliminated when T < c N / e; consistent otherwise. The bound is PROVED FROM Haldane's accounting, which is itself a named hypothesis the module never proves and which has been contested since 1957 (soft selection, truncation selection and standing variation all change c); a candidate that does not accept it is not ruled on
list.canEliminate: a claim that accepts Haldane's cost model and still asks for more substitutions than its reproductive excess can pay for

kernelChecked: That the hypothesis HaldaneCost N T e c (N <= e T / c, c > 0, e >= 0) with e > 0 implies T >= c N / e, and that a time below c N / e contradicts it.
assumed: Haldane 1957's cost accounting itself, which is NOT proved here and has been contested since publication (soft selection, truncation selection, standing variation and linked substitutions all change the cost).
A value for the cost per substitution c and the reproductive excess e; the project supplies neither for any real population.
That the candidate accepts the accounting: one that rejects it is not ruled on.

list.property: whether a committed mass exponent lies in the band the project's own fitted studies span
list.rule: eliminated when the committed exponent interval is disjoint from [2.90, 3.02]; the certificate shows no member of the measured band has that exponent. CONDITIONAL on the observation: a reader who rejects E2 drops this elimination and keeps every proved one
list.canEliminate: a design committing a mass exponent no fitted flying-fish study supports
list.faithfulness: not assessed (no paper states this form)

list.property: whether the power required exceeds the ceiling of every teleost in the measured ranges
list.rule: eliminated when the committed power required exceeds 0.0458 W, the largest sustained aerobic ceiling the measured ranges allow at 0.06 kg. Stronger than C14, which rules only on the particular proxies a candidate commits; CONDITIONAL on E3
list.canEliminate: any claim of sustained aerobic flight at this mass above the ceiling of every teleost the measured record allows
list.faithfulness: not assessed (no paper states this form)

list.property: whether the O2 store carried into the air can pay for the claimed flight
list.rule: eliminated when the claimed power exceeds E S / t, the mean aerobic power the store allows over the claimed duration; CONDITIONAL on E4. Bounds the aerobic part only: burst power on white-muscle stores is outside it
list.canEliminate: a long powered flight on a store too small to pay for it aerobically
list.faithfulness: not assessed (no paper states this form)

list.property: whether the animal is alive at the stage the phenotype is scored
list.rule: eliminated when the source reports death at or before the scoring stage; CONDITIONAL on E7 and on the times the source states. Lethality of a homozygote says nothing about a heterozygote, a mosaic, a conditional allele or a rescue
list.canEliminate: a design that claims a phenotype from a lever whose animal does not reach the stage at which the phenotype exists
list.faithfulness: not assessed (no paper states this form)

list.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
list.property: the log-log exponent of weight on a linear dimension under isometric scaling
list.rule: eliminated when the committed exponent interval excludes 3
list.canEliminate: a candidate that asserts isometry and a measured exponent whose interval excludes 3 (for example every NHANES window in the claims thread's test, if read as isometric)

kernelChecked: If W L = k L^3 for all L > 0 with k > 0, then for L1 ≠ L2 the log-log slope (log W L2 − log W L1)/(log L2 − log L1) equals exactly 3 (cubeLaw_loglog_exponent) and W L2 / W L1 = (L2/L1)^3 (cubeLaw_ratio).
Contrapositive: two sizes with a log-log slope b ≠ 3 rule out W = k L^3 for every k (not_cubeLaw_of_exponent_ne_three).
assumed: A single linear dimension L and mass W of one body family; fixed shape and constant density are what W = k L^3 encodes.
Thompson's "mainly (though not wholly)" is not formalised: the theorem is exact, the law is approximate, and the tolerance band [2.5, 3.5] the claim test uses is a decision rule outside the module.
No data enters the module; the measured exponents are read from the claims thread's result files and pointed to.

ledger.problem: Why are all leaves the size they are, and not an order of magnitude larger or smaller? How is the upper limit on leaf size set?
ledger.description: A leaf scaled isometrically by k: blade area ~ k^2, blade mass ~ k^3 (thickness scales too), petiole cross-section ~ k^2; petiole bending stress ~ (mass x lever arm)/section modulus ~ k^4/k^3 = k; the upper limit is where this stress reaches petiole strength.
notFormalised: the value of the petiole size limit (sigma_max and the shape constants are not supplied); wind loading (dynamic) is outside R9

meta.checkable_rationale: Isometric mass vs cross-section scaling.
meta.reading: 'Blade mass ~ k^3 (thickness scales too)' is the body-like load of R9a (C7b, exponent 3); 'petiole cross-section ~ k^2' is C2a; 'petiole bending stress ~ (mass x lever arm)/section modulus ~ k^4/k^3 = k' is exactly R9a conclusion 1 (C12, exponent 1), so the candidate is consistent, not eliminated; 'the upper limit is where this stress reaches petiole strength' is the existence of L_max,b (bending_cannot_carry), whose value needs sigma_max and the shape constants. The candidate chose the R9a fork by committing to thickness scaling; under R9b (constant thickness) no limit would follow.

summary.headline: Of 152 theorems, 35 hold when instantiated on the flying fish (the blueprint certificate's 11 structural theorems, the exact minimum-speed bound on the Park and Choi specimen, the cube law approximately on Davenport's exponent, and 19 bookkeeping lemmas), 14 have their isometry hypotheses violated by Davenport's within-species exponents (fin area 1.834 vs 2, wing loading 1.236 vs 1), and 103 cannot be evaluated because an input is missing: a neutral substitution rate or fixation probability for the family, fitness variance at any locus, an asexual lineage (none known), material strength and section data for fin rays and bone, muscle fraction and power, and v_min or L/D at a second body size.
notMeasuredForExocoetidae: mutation rate (proxy from herring and stickleback)
effective population size for the family (one mitochondrial Ne for E. volitans)
breaking stress and cross-sections of fin rays or bone
muscle mass fraction and mass-specific power
v_min, L/D or C_L,max at more than one body size
confidence intervals on the Davenport 1992 exponents (abstract only)

empirical.framing: An observation is not a mathematical truth, so this layer declares NO axiom. Each entry is a Lean structure whose fields are the measured numbers and whose proof obligations are the inequalities the observation asserts; a theorem that needs an observation takes the structure as an argument, exactly as the scaling modules take AreaLaw and CubeLaw. #print axioms therefore still reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for every theorem in the development (lean/Delphi/Audit.lean). Status "empirical" is distinct from "proved": a reader may reject an entry, and the ledger says which eliminations were conditional on it.

nonVacuity.why: An inconsistent set of observations would let the checker eliminate every candidate, and that failure would look exactly like success. The witness instantiates every entry with the project's measured numbers at once; if two entries contradicted each other it would not type-check.
nonVacuity.mutation: lean/mutate.mjs: empirical-witness-outside-band moves a band so the measured value falls outside it, and the witness must then fail to compile.

entries.title: Isometry fails within a species
entries.statement: areaExponent < 2 and 1 < wingLoadingExponent, with the mass exponent in [2.90, 3.02].
entries.observation: Within one species, pectoral fin area grows as SL^1.834 and wing loading as SL^1.236 (mass as SL^2.981): fin area falls behind the isometric square and wing loading outruns the isometric first power, so a bigger fish of the same species is more heavily loaded than isometry predicts.
entries.source: physics/allometry.json (Davenport 1992, as the physics thread recorded it)

entries.note: the abstract calls growth in mass negatively allometric; 2.981 is just below the isometric 3

entries.quantity: lateral fin area vs standard length
entries.note: below the isometric 2: fins grow relatively smaller as the fish grows

entries.taxa: Exocoetus obtusirostris, one species, within-species regressions (the exponents are the three 'vs standard length' entries of the file)
entries.scope: Three separate regressions, no confidence intervals, and NOT mutually consistent: 2.981 - 1.834 = 1.147 against the fitted 1.236. That inconsistency is why C13 needs intervals, and it is the reason nine audit rows read "violated" rather than a defect of those theorems.
entries.usedBy: the flying-fish audit (lean/AUDIT-FLYING-FISH.md): the rows whose isometry hypotheses this observation contradicts
entries.rejectable: Reject it and the audit rows that read "violated" become "cannot evaluate"; nothing proved elsewhere changes.

entries.title: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
entries.statement: 2.90 <= b <= 3.02; hence for a weight following one power law, r^2.90 <= W(L2)/W(L1) <= r^3.02 when r = L2/L1 >= 1.
entries.observation: The 6 fitted field length-weight studies of 5 flying-fish species in the project's own table give exponents from 2.908 to 3.011.
entries.source: physics/length-weight.csv (FishBase length-weight list page, rows with a locality and n)

excluded.why: a male-only fit far below every other row; named here rather than silently dropped

entries.taxa: Cheilopogon atrisignis; Cheilopogon unicolor; Cypselurus poecilopterus; Hirundichthys affinis (female); Hirundichthys affinis (mixed); Hirundichthys oxycephalus
entries.scope: The 1 male-only row (Hirundichthys affinis, b = 2.208) is EXCLUDED and named: including it would widen the band to 2.21. Length types differ across rows (SL, FL, TL) and the FishBase page does not show the references. Eighteen further rows with b exactly 3.000 and n of 2 to 6 are unverified estimates and are not used.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and a scaled design's weight is unconstrained by the record; the exact cube law (C7b) still rules under isometry.

entries.title: Efficiency, cardiac output and arterial O2 lie in the measured teleost ranges
entries.statement: eta <= 0.15, oxycaloric <= 19.35 J/ml, cardiac output <= 0.075 ml/s and arterial O2 <= 0.21 ml/ml imply an aerobic ceiling of at most 0.0458 W.
entries.observation: No teleost in the ranges the physiology chain cites has a sustained aerobic ceiling above 0.0458 W at the measured mass (0.06 kg). This is what makes the C14 eliminations binding: they hold for every animal the measured record allows, not only for one choice of proxies.
entries.source: physiology/muscle.js (efficiency, oxycaloric), physiology/cardiac.js (cardiac output range), physiology/haemoglobin.js (blood O2 capacity), as cited in lean/eliminate/physiology-candidates.json

from.efficiency: efficiency: { value: 0.15, kind: 'proxy', species: 'Salmo salar (ventricular muscle)', source: 'gamperl2021: efficiency of ventricular muscle ~15% in salmon (7% in char); trout ventricle 15-25% (Harwood et al. 2002, cited there). No fetched value for fish skeletal muscle, so cardiac muscle is used.'
from.oxycaloric: oxycalorific_J_per_mgO2: { value: 13.54, kind: 'secondary', source: 'gerry2014 (Fig. 1 legend): "oxycaloric value of 13.54 J mg-1 O2" citing their ref. 89' }
from.cardiacRange: Q_range_ml_min_kg: { value: [20, 75], kind: 'secondary', species: 'O. mykiss', source: 'gerry2014 Discussion: ventral aortic flow-cuff values ~20 at rest to ~75 ml/min/kg maximum (citing refs)' }
from.haemoglobinCapacity: cap_ml_per_ml: { value: (4 * 0.9 * 22.4) / 1000, kind: 'proxy', species: 'Oncorhynchus mykiss', source: 'derived from rummer2015 Table 1 [Hb] 0.9 mM per tetramer (Hct standardised to ~25%): 4 x 0.9 mmol/l x 22.4 ml/mmol = 0.0806 ml O2/ml' }

entries.taxa: Every value is a PROXY from another teleost: Salmo salar ventricular muscle (efficiency), Lutjanus apodus and Oncorhynchus mykiss (cardiac output), Oncorhynchus mykiss (blood O2). No Exocoetidae physiology exists in this project.
entries.scope: The bound is an upper bound at one mass, and the cardiac output ceiling is the maximum of a secondary range (20 to 75 ml/min/kg, gerry2014 Discussion). It bounds SUSTAINED AEROBIC power only: burst power on white-muscle stores is outside it, and that is what a flying fish is understood to use. Scaling it to another mass requires the cardiac output per kg, not this number.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and C14 still rules, but only on the particular proxies a candidate commits, not on every teleost.

entries.title: Gills do not ventilate in air
entries.statement: uptakeInAir = 0; hence over a flight of duration t the mean aerobic power is at most E S / t for an O2 store S.
entries.observation: O2 uptake is zero while airborne, so airborne aerobic work is paid for out of the store carried into the air, and the airborne aerobic ceiling falls as the flight lengthens.
entries.source: physiology/index.js (the chain sets uptake to zero in air) and its self-test, where the store drains
entries.taxa: A property of the gill as a water-breathing organ, not of a species; the chain applies it to its flying-fish model.
entries.scope: Bounds the AEROBIC part only, and takes the store and the oxycaloric equivalent as inputs: neither is measured for Exocoetidae here. Cutaneous and buccal exchange in air are not modelled, and burst (anaerobic) power is outside it.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and the airborne ceiling is whatever the circulation can deliver, i.e. C14 with no time limit.

entries.title: The observed pectoral/SL range
entries.statement: 0.406 <= pectoral/SL <= 0.823 for a measured specimen; a design outside the range is above or below it.
entries.observation: Across 49 flying-fish specimens, pectoral fin length over standard length runs from 0.406 to 0.823, median 0.687 (standard lengths 1.68 to 24 cm).
entries.taxa: Beloniform museum specimens: flying fish only in this entry (the file also records flying halfbeaks 0.175-0.388, halfbeaks 0.115-0.177, needlefish 0.071-0.106).
entries.scope: A statement about the RECORD. A design outside the range is outside everything measured, which is weaker than impossible, and no theorem here says such a fish cannot exist. Preserved museum specimens, lengths only: no mass, no fin area, no glide data. It is deliberately NOT a constraint in the ledger, so that nothing is ever reported as eliminated by it; it is a flag in the Design Studio.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and the Studio loses a provenance flag; no verdict anywhere changes.

entries.title: "required for" is never propagated down part_of
entries.statement: No row of the map whose link type is "required for" is derived by propagating a link down a part_of edge.
entries.observation: Not an observation at all: a rule this project adopted for building the genotype map (the hub's idea-gp-propagation-rules). A gene required for a whole need not be required for each part.
entries.source: the genotype map's own propagation_rules (genotype/map.vetted.json) and the hub's adopted rule
entries.taxa: none: a rule about the map, not about animals
entries.scope: A convention, so it can be wrong only in the sense of being a bad choice. Labelled as such wherever it appears, and it licenses no biological conclusion.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and the map may carry downward "required for" links; the closure check (G2) then propagates an edit to more nodes, not fewer.

entries.title: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
entries.statement: death_hpf <= scored_hpf implies the phenotype cannot be scored in a living animal.
entries.observation: Two levers in the project's own intervention table state both times: ezh2 dies at 48 hpf, the stage at which its fin absence is scored, and wls dies by 12 dpf while the ray parameters exist only from 45 dpf.
entries.source: genotype/interventions.json (the genotype thread's own lethality notes, quoted in the value)

evaluated.quote: LETHAL: 'die around 2 days post fertilization' / 'They die at 48 hpf'. The animal dies at the same stage at which the fin phenotype is scored, before any fin skeletal differentiation.

LETHAL BEFORE THE RAY PARAMETER EXISTS: 'The mutants fail to develop swim bladders and die by approximately 12 dpf.' Lepidotrichia are not formed by then, so no ray length, segment or branching value can be measured in this allele, and the effect_size value is null for that reason. Even fully rescued mutants 'did not survive to adulthood'.
evaluated.conversion: death "by approximately 12 dpf" = 288 h; the ray parameters exist only from Juvenile:Days 45-89, taken as 45 dpf = 1080 h

notEvaluated.why: the genotype thread records lethality as free text (58 rows say "not reported"); only rows that state BOTH a time of death and a scoring stage in hours are instantiated here, and no time is parsed out of prose beyond those two

entries.taxa: Danio rerio (zebrafish) alleles and treatments; nothing here is measured on a flying fish.
entries.scope: Only the 2 rows that state both a death time and a scoring stage in hours are instantiated. the genotype thread records lethality as free text (58 rows say "not reported"); only rows that state BOTH a time of death and a scoring stage in hours are instantiated here, and no time is parsed out of prose beyond those two Lethality of a homozygote says nothing about a heterozygote, a mosaic, a conditional allele or a rescue, and a lever lethal in zebrafish may not be in another species.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and a design may claim a phenotype from a lever whose animal does not reach the stage; nothing proved elsewhere changes.

entries.status: not an empirical entry: already proved
entries.title: A part cannot appear before its precursor
entries.statement: Every develops_from edge goes strictly later in stage, and the relation is acyclic.
entries.observation: The stages are data (ZFIN); the ordering is a THEOREM about that data, certified by a kernel evaluation on the fin subtree. Restating it as an empirical hypothesis would weaken a theorem into an assumption, so it is not in this layer.
entries.taxa: Danio rerio anatomy (ZFA), joined to the blueprint by cross-reference
entries.scope: See the law genotype-developmental-ordering in lean/laws.json.
entries.rejectable: The ZFIN stage order is the assumption; reject it and the certificate says nothing.
